title.zh: 卷38 刁雍 王慧龍 韓延之 袁式
title.en: Volume 38: Diao Yong, Wang Huilong, Han Yanzhi, Yuan Shi
title.raw: 卷38 刁雍 王慧龍 韓延之 袁式 Volume 38: Diao Yong, Wang Huilong, Han Yanzhi, Yuan Shi

sentences.zh: 刁雍 王慧龍 韓延之 袁式

translations.literal: Diao Yong, Wang Huilong, Han Yanzhi, Yuan Shi
translations.idiomatic: Diao Yong, Wang Huilong, Han Yanzhi, and Yuan Shi

sentences.zh: 刁雍，字淑和，勃海饒安人也。

translations.literal: Diao Yong, styled Shuhe, was a man of Raoyan in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Yong, whose courtesy name was Shuhe, was a native of Raoyan in Bohai Commandery.

sentences.zh: 高祖攸，晉御史中丞。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather You was Jin Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather You served Jin as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 曾祖協，從司馬叡渡江，居于京口，位至尚書令。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Xie followed Sima Rui in crossing the Yangzi, dwelt at Jingkou, and rose to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Xie crossed the Yangzi with Sima Rui, settled at Jingkou, and eventually reached the post of Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 父暢，司馬德宗右衞將軍。

translations.literal: His father Chang was Sima Dezong's Right Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chang served Emperor An of Jin as Right Guard General.

sentences.zh: 初，暢兄逵以劉裕輕狡薄行，負社錢三萬，違時不還，執而徵焉。

translations.literal: At first, Chang's elder brother Kui, because Liu Yu was frivolous, cunning, and of shallow conduct, owed thirty thousand in communal funds and failed to repay when due, was seized and levied upon.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Chang's elder brother Kui had denounced Liu Yu as frivolous, cunning, and morally shallow. Kui owed thirty thousand in communal funds and, when he failed to repay on time, was arrested and pressed for payment.

sentences.zh: 及裕誅桓玄，以嫌故先誅刁氏。

translations.literal: When Yu executed Huan Xuan, because of enmity he first executed the Diao clan.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu overthrew Huan Xuan, he took the old grudge as a pretext and wiped out the Diao family first.

sentences.zh: 雍為暢故吏所匿，奔姚興豫州牧姚紹於洛陽，後至長安。

translations.literal: Yong was hidden by Chang's former clerks, fled to Yao Xing's Inspector of Yuzhou Yao Shao at Luoyang, and later reached Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was sheltered by his father's former retainers, fled to Yao Shao, Yao Xing's governor of Yuzhou, at Luoyang, and later made his way to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 雍博覽書傳，姚興以雍為太子中庶子。

translations.literal: Yong broadly read books and records; Yao Xing made Yong Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was widely read in the classics and histories, and Yao Xing appointed him Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 泰常二年，姚泓滅，與司馬休之等歸國。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taichang, when Yao Hong was destroyed, he returned to the state together with Sima Xiuzhi and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taichang, after Yao Hong's defeat, he returned to Wei together with Sima Xiuzhi and the others.

sentences.zh: 上表陳誠，於南境自效。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial stating his sincerity, to offer himself on the southern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial pledging his loyalty and offering to serve on the southern border.

sentences.zh: 太宗許之，假雍建義將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Daowu approved it and provisionally made Yong General Who Establishes Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daowu accepted the offer and provisionally appointed Yong General Who Establishes Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 雍遂於河濟之間招集流散，得五千餘人，南阻大

translations.literal: Yong then between the Yellow River and the Ji gathered scattered people, obtaining more than five thousand men, and southward blocked the great
translations.idiomatic: Yong then recruited refugees between the Yellow and Ji rivers, mustering more than five thousand men, and took up a defensive position south of Great

translations.literal: Text lacuna in the manuscript.
translations.idiomatic: Text missing in the manuscript.

sentences.zh: ，[1]擾動徐兗，建牙誓眾，傳檄邊境。

translations.literal: ,[1] disturbing Xu and Yan, raising the command banner and swearing the host, and issuing proclamations to the borderlands.
translations.idiomatic: [1] He stirred up trouble in Xu and Yan, raised his standard to rally the troops, and sent proclamations along the frontier.

sentences.zh: 劉裕遣將李嵩等討雍，雍斬之於蒙山。

translations.literal: Liu Yu sent the generals Li Song and others to attack Yong; Yong beheaded him at Mount Meng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu sent his generals Li Song and others against Yong, and Yong killed Li Song on Mount Meng.

sentences.zh: 於是眾至二萬，進屯固山。

translations.literal: Thereupon his host reached twenty thousand, and he advanced to encamp at Mount Gu.
translations.idiomatic: His forces then grew to twenty thousand, and he advanced to camp on Mount Gu.

sentences.zh: 七年三月，雍從弟彌亦率眾入京口，規共討裕，裕遣兵破之。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventh year, Yong's younger cousin Mi also led troops into Jingkou, planning together to attack Yu; Yu sent troops and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the seventh year, Yong's younger cousin Mi also led his men into Jingkou, intending to join forces against Liu Yu, but Yu sent troops and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 六月，雍又侵裕青州，雍敗，乃收散卒保於馬耳山。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Yong again invaded Yu's Qing province; Yong was defeated, then gathered scattered soldiers and held Mount Ma'er.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Yong again invaded Liu Yu's Qing province, was defeated, and withdrew with his scattered troops to hold Mount Ma'er.

sentences.zh: 又為裕青州軍所逼，遂入大鄉山。

translations.literal: Again pressed by Yu's Qing province army, he then entered Mount Daxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed again by Liu Yu's Qingzhou forces, he retreated into Mount Daxiang.

sentences.zh: 八年，太宗南幸鄴，朝於行觀。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Emperor Daowu went south to Ye and attended court at the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Emperor Daowu traveled south to Ye, and Yong presented himself at the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: [2]問：「先聞卿家縛劉裕，於卿親疏？

translations.literal: [2] He asked: "I earlier heard that your family bound Liu Yu—how close is he to you in kinship?"
translations.idiomatic: [2] The emperor asked, "I have heard that your family once had Liu Yu bound. How close is he to you by kinship?"

sentences.zh: 」雍曰：「是臣伯父。

translations.literal: " Yong said: "He is this subject's uncle."
translations.idiomatic: Yong replied, "He is my uncle."

sentences.zh: 」太宗笑曰：「劉裕父子當應憚卿。

translations.literal: " Emperor Daowu laughed and said: "Liu Yu and his son ought to fear you."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daowu laughed and said, "Liu Yu and his son ought to fear you."

sentences.zh: 」又謂之曰：「朕先遣叔孫建等攻青州，民盡藏避，城猶未下。

translations.literal: " He further said to him: "We earlier sent Tuoba Jian and others to attack Qing province; the people all hid and fled, yet the city still was not taken."
translations.idiomatic: He went on, "I earlier sent Tuoba Jian and others to attack Qing province. The people all hid and fled, yet the city still has not fallen."

sentences.zh: 彼既素憚卿威，士民又相信服，今欲遣卿助建等，卿宜勉之。

translations.literal: They have long feared your prestige, and the gentry and commoners again trust and submit; now We wish to send you to assist Jian and the others—you should exert yourself."
translations.idiomatic: They have long feared your reputation, and the local gentry and commoners trust you as well. I now wish to send you to assist Jian and the others. You should do your utmost."

sentences.zh: 」於是假雍鎮東將軍、青州刺史、東光侯，給五萬騎，使別立義軍。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he provisionally made Yong General Who Pacifies the East, Inspector of Qing province, and Marquis of Dongguang, gave him fifty thousand horsemen, and had him separately raise a righteous army.
translations.idiomatic: He then provisionally appointed Yong General Who Pacifies the East, Inspector of Qing province, and Marquis of Dongguang, granted him fifty thousand cavalry, and ordered him to raise a separate volunteer force.

sentences.zh: 建先攻東陽，雍至，招集義眾，得五千人。

translations.literal: Jian first attacked Dongyang; when Yong arrived, he gathered righteous followers and obtained five thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Jian had already begun the assault on Dongyang. When Yong arrived, he recruited volunteers and mustered five thousand men.

sentences.zh: 遣撫慰郡縣，土人盡下，送租供軍。

translations.literal: He sent them to reassure the commanderies and counties; the local people all submitted, and sent rent to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: He sent them out to reassure the commanderies and counties. The local people all came down from hiding and sent in rent grain to supply the army.

sentences.zh: 是時攻東陽，平其北城三十許步。

translations.literal: At that time they attacked Dongyang and leveled its north wall some thirty paces.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the assault on Dongyang had leveled some thirty paces of the north wall.

sentences.zh: 劉義符青州刺史竺夔於城內鑿地道，南下入澠水澗，以為退路。

translations.literal: Liu Yifu's Inspector of Qing province Zhu Kui inside the city dug an underground passage southward into the Mian River ravine as a route of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yifu's Qingzhou inspector Zhu Kui dug a tunnel inside the city leading south into the Mian River ravine to secure a line of retreat.

sentences.zh: 雍謂建曰：「此城已平，[3]宜時入取。

translations.literal: Yong said to Jian: "This city is already level;[3] you should enter and take it at once."
translations.idiomatic: Yong told Jian, "The north wall is already breached.[3] You should enter and take the city immediately."

sentences.zh: 不者走盡。

translations.literal: Otherwise they will all flee.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the defenders will all escape."

sentences.zh: 」建懼傷兵士，難之。

translations.literal: " Jian, fearing injury to the soldiers, found it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Jian, fearing casualties among his troops, hesitated.

sentences.zh: 雍曰：「若懼傷官兵者，雍今請將義兵先入。

translations.literal: Yong said: "If you fear injuring the government troops, Yong now asks to lead the righteous army in first."
translations.idiomatic: Yong said, "If you fear losses among the regular troops, I ask to lead the volunteers in first."

sentences.zh: 」建不聽。

translations.literal: " Jian would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Jian refused.

sentences.zh: 夔欲東走，會義符遣其將檀道濟等救青州。

translations.literal: Kui wished to flee east, but it happened that Yifu sent his generals Tan Daoji and others to rescue Qing province.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Kui was preparing to break out to the east when Liu Yifu sent his generals Tan Daoji and others to relieve Qing province.

sentences.zh: 雍謂建曰：「賊畏官軍突騎，以鎖連車為函陣。

translations.literal: Yong said to Jian: "The rebels fear the government army's shock cavalry and use chained wagons to form a box formation."
translations.idiomatic: Yong told Jian, "The enemy fears our shock cavalry and has chained their wagons together into a wagon-fort formation."

sentences.zh: 大峴已南，處處狹隘，不得方軌。

translations.literal: South of Great Xian Pass, everywhere is narrow and cramped, and they cannot deploy in full formation.
translations.idiomatic: South of Great Xian Pass the terrain is narrow everywhere, and they cannot march in full formation.

sentences.zh: 雍求將義兵五千，要嶮破之。

translations.literal: Yong asked to lead five thousand righteous troops and strike them at the defiles to break them.
translations.idiomatic: Yong asked to take five thousand volunteers and ambush them at the narrow passes to break their formation."

sentences.zh: 」建不聽曰：「兵人不宜水土，疫病過半。

translations.literal: " Jian would not listen and said: "The soldiers are unsuited to the climate and water; more than half are sick."
translations.idiomatic: Jian refused and said, "The men cannot endure the climate and water here. More than half are sick with disease."

sentences.zh: 若相持不休，兵自死盡，何須復戰。

translations.literal: If we hold on without end, the troops will die off on their own—why must we fight again?
translations.idiomatic: If we keep holding on, the army will waste away on its own. Why fight further?

sentences.zh: 今不損大軍，安全而返，計之上也。

translations.literal: Now not harming the main army and returning safely is the best plan."
translations.idiomatic: The best plan now is to withdraw without damaging the main force and return safely."

sentences.zh: 」建乃引還。

translations.literal: " Jian then led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Jian then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 雍遂鎮尹卯固。

translations.literal: Yong then garrisoned Yimao Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Yong then took up his post at Yimao Fort.

sentences.zh: 又詔令南入，以亂賊境。

translations.literal: He was again ordered by edict to enter the south and throw the enemy territory into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: He was again ordered by imperial edict to push south and harass the enemy borderlands.

sentences.zh: 雍攻克項城。

translations.literal: Yong captured Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yong captured Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 會有敕追令隨機立效，雍於是招集譙、梁、彭、沛民五千餘家，置二十七營，遷鎮濟陰。

translations.literal: It happened that an edict urgently ordered him to achieve results as circumstances allowed; Yong thereupon gathered more than five thousand households from the people of Qiao, Liang, Peng, and Pei, established twenty-seven camps, and moved his garrison to Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: An urgent edict then arrived ordering him to seize whatever opportunity presented itself. Yong gathered more than five thousand households from Qiao, Liang, Peng, and Pei, organized them into twenty-seven camps, and transferred his headquarters to Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 延和二年，立徐州於外黃城，置譙、梁、彭、沛四郡九縣，以雍為平南將軍、徐州刺史，賜爵東安侯。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yanhe, Xu province was established at Waihuang city, with four commanderies and nine counties of Qiao, Liang, Peng, and Pei set up; Yong was made General Who Pacifies the South, Inspector of Xu province, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Dong'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yanhe Xu province was established at Waihuang, with the four commanderies of Qiao, Liang, Peng, and Pei and nine counties placed under its administration. Yong was appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Xu province and enfeoffed as Marquis of Dong'an.

sentences.zh: 在鎮七年，太延四年，徵還京師，頻歲為邊民所請。

translations.literal: After seven years in the garrison, in the fourth year of Taiyan he was summoned back to the capital; for successive years the border people had petitioned for him.
translations.idiomatic: After seven years in command, in the fourth year of Taiyan he was recalled to the capital, though for years the frontier populace had petitioned to keep him there.

sentences.zh: 世祖嘉之，真君二年復授使持節、侍中、都督揚豫兗徐四州諸軍事、征南將軍、徐豫二州刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu commended this; in the second year of Zhenjun he again invested him with the Staff of Authority, made him Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Yang, Yu, Yan, and Xu provinces, General Who Campaigns South, and Inspector of Xu and Yu provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu praised this loyalty, and in the second year of Zhenjun again appointed him Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Yang, Yu, Yan, and Xu, General Who Campaigns South, and Inspector of Xu and Yu.

sentences.zh: 三年，劉義隆將裴方明寇陷仇池，詔雍與建興公古弼等十餘將討平之。

translations.literal: In the third year, Liu Yilong's general Pei Fangming invaded and captured Chouchi; an edict ordered Yong, Duke of Jianxing Gu Bibi, and more than ten other generals to suppress and pacify it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Liu Yilong's general Pei Fangming invaded and captured Chouchi. An edict ordered Yong, Duke of Jianxing Gu Bibi, and more than a dozen other commanders to suppress and pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 五年，以本將軍為薄骨律鎮將。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, with his former rank he became Garrison Commander of Bugulai.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was appointed Garrison Commander of Bugulai while retaining his former rank.

sentences.zh: 至鎮，表曰：

translations.literal: On reaching the garrison, he submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his post he submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 臣蒙寵出鎮，奉辭西藩，總統諸軍，戶口殷廣。

translations.literal: This subject, receiving favor, went out to garrison, took leave of the western frontier, and commands all armies; households are numerous and broad.
translations.idiomatic: I have received the grace of appointment to this frontier post on the western border, where I command all forces and oversee a large population.

sentences.zh: 又總勒戎馬，以防不虞，督課諸屯，以為儲積。

translations.literal: I also command troops and horses to guard against the unexpected, and supervise the garrison farms to serve as stored provisions.
translations.idiomatic: I also command the troops and horses to guard against emergencies and supervise the garrison farms to build up reserves.

sentences.zh: 夙夜惟憂，不遑寧處。

translations.literal: From dawn to night I only worry and have no leisure to rest at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night I worry over these duties and have scarcely a moment's peace.

sentences.zh: 以今年四月末到鎮，時以夏中，不及東作。

translations.literal: I reached the garrison at the end of the fourth month this year; it was already midsummer and too late for spring planting.
translations.idiomatic: I reached my post at the end of the fourth month this year, but by then it was already midsummer and too late for spring planting.

sentences.zh: 念彼農夫，雖復布野，官渠乏水，不得廣殖。

translations.literal: Thinking of those farmers, though fields again spread across the wilds, the official canals lack water and they cannot plant broadly.
translations.idiomatic: I think of the farmers here: though fields stretch across the countryside, the official canals lack water and they cannot plant on a large scale.

sentences.zh: 乘前以來，功不充課，兵人口累，率皆飢儉。

translations.literal: Riding on what came before, labor does not meet quotas; soldiers and commoners accumulate, and on the whole all suffer hunger.
translations.idiomatic: For years the work quotas have gone unmet, and soldiers and civilians alike are for the most part hungry and destitute.

sentences.zh: 略加檢行，知此土稼穡艱難。

translations.literal: After a brief inspection tour, I know that in this land sowing and reaping are difficult.
translations.idiomatic: After a brief inspection I have learned how hard agriculture is in this region.

sentences.zh: 夫欲育民豐國，事須大田。

translations.literal: Now, to nurture the people and enrich the state, affairs require great fields.
translations.idiomatic: To nourish the people and enrich the state, one must rely on large-scale farming.

sentences.zh: 此土乏雨，正以引河為用。

translations.literal: This land lacks rain and must just use drawing the river.
translations.idiomatic: This region lacks rain and must depend on drawing water from the river.

sentences.zh: 觀舊渠堰，乃是上古所制，非近代也。

translations.literal: Observing the old canals and weirs, they were made in high antiquity and are not recent.
translations.idiomatic: The old canals and weirs I have inspected were built in high antiquity, not in recent times.

sentences.zh: 富平西南三十里，有艾山，南北二十六里，東西四十五里，鑿以通河，似禹舊迹。

translations.literal: Thirty li southwest of Fuping is Mount Ai, twenty-six li north to south and forty-five li east to west, cut through to connect with the river, resembling Yu's old traces.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty li southwest of Fuping stands Mount Ai, twenty-six li from north to south and forty-five li from east to west, cut through to connect with the river in what appears to be a trace of Yu the Great's works.

sentences.zh: 其兩岸作溉田大渠，廣十餘步，山南引水入此渠中。

translations.literal: On both banks they made a great canal for irrigated fields, more than ten paces wide, drawing water from south of the mountain into this canal.
translations.idiomatic: On both banks they built a great irrigation canal more than ten paces wide, drawing water from the south side of the mountain into it.

sentences.zh: 計昔為之，高於水不過一丈。

translations.literal: Calculating how it was made in the past, it was no more than one zhang above the water.
translations.idiomatic: When it was first built, it stood no more than one zhang above the water level.

sentences.zh: [4]河水激急，沙土漂流，今日此渠高於河水二丈三尺，又河水浸射，往往崩頹。

translations.literal: [4] The river water is swift and urgent, sand and soil drift away; today this canal is two zhang and three chi above the river water, and again the river water shoots and soaks in, often collapsing and crumbling.
translations.idiomatic: [4] The river runs swift, carrying off sand and silt. Today this canal stands two zhang and three chi above the river, while the river itself erodes and undermines it, so that sections often collapse.

sentences.zh: 渠溉高懸，水不得上。

translations.literal: The canal irrigation hangs high; water cannot be raised up.
translations.idiomatic: The irrigation channel now hangs too high for water to be drawn up into it.

sentences.zh: 雖復諸處案舊引水，水亦難求。

translations.literal: Though again at various places they followed the old method of drawing water, water is also hard to obtain.
translations.idiomatic: Even where people follow the old methods of drawing water, little can be obtained.

sentences.zh: 今艾山北，河中有洲渚，水分為二。

translations.literal: Now north of Mount Ai, in the river there are islets and shoals, and the water divides in two.
translations.idiomatic: North of Mount Ai the river now contains shoals that divide the current in two.

sentences.zh: 西河小狹，水廣百四十步。

translations.literal: The western river is small and narrow; the water is one hundred forty paces wide.
translations.idiomatic: The western channel is narrow, only about one hundred forty paces across.

sentences.zh: 臣今求入來年正月，於河西高渠之北八里、分河之下五里，平地鑿渠，廣十五步，深五尺，築其兩岸，令高一丈。

translations.literal: This subject now asks to enter the first month of next year, eight li north of the High Canal on the west bank of the river and five li below where the river divides, to cut a canal on level ground fifteen paces wide and five chi deep, and build both banks one zhang high.
translations.idiomatic: I ask permission to begin work in the first month of next year: eight li north of the High Canal on the west bank and five li below the river's division point, to cut a level canal fifteen paces wide and five chi deep, with banks built up one zhang high.

sentences.zh: 北行四十里，還入古高渠，即循高渠而北，復八十里，合百二十里，大有良田。

translations.literal: Going north forty li, it returns into the ancient High Canal; then following the High Canal north another eighty li, totaling one hundred twenty li, there is much good farmland.
translations.idiomatic: Running north forty li it would rejoin the old High Canal; following that canal north another eighty li makes one hundred twenty li in all, opening a vast tract of fertile land.

sentences.zh: 計用四千人，四十日功，渠得成訖。

translations.literal: Calculated to use four thousand men for forty days' labor, the canal can be completed.
translations.idiomatic: The project would require four thousand laborers for forty days to complete the canal.

sentences.zh: 所欲鑿新渠口，河下五尺，水不得入。

translations.literal: Where the new canal mouth is to be cut, the river is five chi lower, and water cannot enter.
translations.idiomatic: At the point where the new intake is to be cut, the river lies five chi lower, so water cannot flow in.

sentences.zh: 今求從小河東南岸斜斷到西北岸，計長二百七十步，廣十步，高二丈，絕斷小河。

translations.literal: Now I ask to cut diagonally from the small river's southeast bank to the northwest bank, calculated at two hundred seventy paces long, ten paces wide, and two zhang high, cutting off the small river completely.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore propose to cut a diagonal dam from the southeast bank of the lesser channel to the northwest bank, two hundred seventy paces long, ten paces wide, and two zhang high, to block the lesser channel entirely.

sentences.zh: 二十日功，計得成畢，合計用功六十日。

translations.literal: Twenty days' labor, calculated to be completed, totaling sixty days of labor altogether.
translations.idiomatic: That dam would take twenty days to finish, making sixty days of labor in all.

sentences.zh: 小河之水，盡入新渠，水則充足，溉官私田四萬餘頃。

translations.literal: The small river's water would all enter the new canal; water would then be ample and irrigate more than forty thousand qing of official and private fields.
translations.idiomatic: All the water of the lesser channel would flow into the new canal, providing ample irrigation for more than forty thousand qing of public and private fields.

sentences.zh: 一旬之間，則水一遍，水凡四溉，穀得成實。

translations.literal: Within one ten-day period the water would pass once; water altogether four irrigations, and grain would achieve full fruit.
translations.idiomatic: Within each ten-day period the fields could be watered once, and with four irrigations in all the grain would ripen fully.

sentences.zh: 官課常充，民亦豐贍。

translations.literal: Official levies would constantly be filled, and the people also would be abundant and provided for.
translations.idiomatic: Government quotas would be met regularly, and the people would enjoy abundance.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「卿憂國愛民，知欲更引河水，勸課大田。

translations.literal: An edict said: "You worry for the state and love the people, know you wish again to draw river water and urge great fields."
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: "You care for the state and love the people. I see that you wish to draw the river anew and promote large-scale farming.

sentences.zh: 宜便興立，以克就為功，何必限其日數也。

translations.literal: You should promptly establish it; take completion as achievement—why must you limit the number of days?"
translations.idiomatic: Begin the work at once and judge success by completion rather than by a fixed number of days."

sentences.zh: 有可以便國利民者，動靜以聞。」

translations.literal: Whatever can benefit the state and profit the people, report your actions and stillness."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever you find further measures that may benefit the state and the people, report them to me at once."

sentences.zh: 七年，雍表曰：「奉詔高平、安定、統萬及臣所守四鎮，出車五千乘，運屯穀五十萬斛付沃野鎮，以供軍糧。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Yong submitted a memorial saying: "Receiving the edict that Gaoping, Anding, Tongwan, and the four garrisons I guard shall dispatch five thousand carts and transport five hundred thousand hu of garrison grain to Woye Garrison to supply army provisions."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Yong submitted another memorial: "By imperial order Gaoping, Anding, Tongwan, and the four garrisons under my command are to dispatch five thousand carts and transport five hundred thousand hu of garrison grain to Woye Garrison for army provisions.

sentences.zh: 臣鎮去沃野八百里，道多深沙，輕車來往，猶以為難，設令載穀，不過二十石，每涉深沙，必致滯陷。

translations.literal: My garrison is eight hundred li from Woye; the road has much deep sand—even light carts going back and forth are still considered difficult. Supposing they load grain, no more than twenty shi; each time they cross deep sand, they necessarily bog down and sink.
translations.idiomatic: My garrison lies eight hundred li from Woye, and the route crosses deep sand. Even light carts find the journey arduous. Loaded with grain, a cart can carry no more than twenty shi, and every crossing of deep sand risks bogging down.

sentences.zh: 又穀在河西，轉至沃野，越度大河，計車五千乘，運十萬斛，百餘日乃得一返，大廢生民耕墾之業。

translations.literal: Again the grain is west of the river, transferred to Woye, crossing the great river; calculated at five thousand carts transporting one hundred thousand hu, more than a hundred days for one return, greatly wasting the people's farming and cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the grain lies west of the river and must be carried to Woye across the great river. Five thousand carts could move only one hundred thousand hu per round trip, and each round would take more than a hundred days, gravely disrupting farming among the common people.

sentences.zh: 車牛艱阻，難可全至，一歲不過二運，五十萬斛乃經三年。

translations.literal: Carts and oxen are hard pressed and obstructed, hard to arrive intact; in one year no more than two transports—the five hundred thousand hu would take three years.
translations.idiomatic: Oxen and carts would suffer heavy losses on the road, and at most two round trips could be made in a year. Delivering five hundred thousand hu would therefore take three years.

sentences.zh: 臣前被詔，有可以便國利民者動靜以聞。

translations.literal: This subject was earlier ordered by edict: whatever can benefit the state and profit the people, report actions and stillness.
translations.idiomatic: I was earlier instructed by edict to report any measure that might benefit the state and the people.

sentences.zh: 臣聞鄭、白之渠，遠引淮海之粟，泝流數千，周年乃得一至，猶稱國有儲糧，民用安樂。

translations.literal: This subject has heard that the canals of Zheng and Bai drew grain from the Huai and sea far away, went upstream thousands of li, and only once a year arrived, yet they were still called having state stored grain and the people's use peaceful and happy.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the Zheng and Bai canals drew grain from the Huai region and the coast, sending it upstream for thousands of li with only one delivery a year, yet the state still enjoyed stored grain and the people lived in comfort.

sentences.zh: 今求於牽屯山河水之次，造船二百艘，二船為一舫，一船勝穀二千斛，一舫十人，計須千人。

translations.literal: Now I ask at Qiantun Mountain beside the river water to build two hundred boats, two boats making one barge, one boat holding two thousand hu of grain, one barge ten men, calculated to need one thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: I propose to build two hundred boats at Qiantun Mountain where the river runs, pairing two boats into each barge. One boat would carry two thousand hu of grain, each barge would need ten men, and the project would require about one thousand workers.

sentences.zh: 臣鎮內之兵，率皆習水。

translations.literal: The soldiers within my garrison, on the whole all are practiced in water.
translations.idiomatic: The troops in my command are for the most part experienced on the water.

sentences.zh: 一運二十萬斛。

translations.literal: One transport two hundred thousand hu.
translations.idiomatic: Each voyage could move two hundred thousand hu.

sentences.zh: 方舟順流，五日而至，自沃野牽上，十日還到，合六十日得一返。

translations.literal: The barges downstream with the current arrive in five days; from Woye towed upstream, ten days to return, totaling sixty days for one round trip.
translations.idiomatic: Going downstream with the current, the barges would reach Woye in five days; towing back upstream would take ten days, for a round trip of sixty days.

sentences.zh: 從三月至九月三返，運送六十萬斛，計用人功，輕於車運十倍有餘，不費牛力，又不廢田。

translations.literal: From the third month to the ninth month three round trips, transporting six hundred thousand hu; calculated in human labor, lighter than cart transport by more than tenfold, not spending ox power, and again not wasting fields.
translations.idiomatic: From the third month through the ninth month three round trips could deliver six hundred thousand hu. The labor required would be more than ten times lighter than cart transport, with no oxen wasted and no farmland abandoned."

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「知欲造船運穀，一冬即成，大省民力，既不費牛，又不廢田，甚善。

translations.literal: " An edict said: "Knowing you wish to build boats and transport grain, completed in one winter, greatly saving the people's strength, neither spending oxen nor wasting fields—very good."
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: "I see that you wish to build boats and transport grain, finishing the fleet in a single winter. This would greatly spare the people's labor, waste no oxen, and abandon no farmland. Excellent.

sentences.zh: 非但一運，自可永以為式。

translations.literal: Not only one transport—it can itself forever serve as a model.
translations.idiomatic: This should serve not only for one shipment but as a permanent model.

sentences.zh: 今別下統萬鎮出兵以供運穀，卿鎮可出百兵為船工，豈可專廢千人？

translations.literal: Now separately order Tongwan Garrison to dispatch troops to supply grain transport; your garrison may send one hundred soldiers as boat workers—how can you exclusively waste one thousand men?"
translations.idiomatic: I shall order Tongwan Garrison separately to provide troops for the transport. Your command may supply one hundred soldiers as shipwrights. Surely you cannot devote a full thousand men to this alone?

sentences.zh: 雖遣船匠，猶須卿指授，未可專任也。

translations.literal: Though boat craftsmen are sent, they still need your instruction and direction; they cannot be solely entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: Even when shipwrights are sent, they will still need your direction and cannot be left entirely on their own.

sentences.zh: 諸有益國利民如此者，續復以聞。」

translations.literal: Whatever benefits the state and profits the people like this, continue again to report."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever you find further measures of this kind that benefit the state and the people, report them to me again."

sentences.zh: 九年，雍表曰：「臣聞安不忘亂，先聖之政也。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Yong submitted a memorial saying: "Your subject has heard that in security one does not forget disorder—this is the governance of the ancient sages.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Yong submitted a memorial: "I have heard that in times of peace one must not forget the danger of chaos—such is the policy of the ancient sages.

sentences.zh: 況綏服之外，帶接邊城，防守不備，無以禦敵者也。

translations.literal: Moreover beyond the pacified regions, bordering and adjoining frontier cities, if defense is not prepared, there is no means to resist the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: How much more so beyond the pacified heartland, where frontier towns lie pressed against one another: if defenses are not ready, there is no way to hold off the enemy.

sentences.zh: 臣鎮所綰河西，爰在邊表，常懼不虞。

translations.literal: The garrison this subject commands oversees Hexi, which lies on the frontier border, and I constantly fear the unforeseen.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison under my command holds Hexi, right on the frontier, and I live in constant fear of sudden attack.

sentences.zh: 平地積穀，實難守護。

translations.literal: Storing grain on open ground is truly hard to defend.
translations.idiomatic: Grain stored on open ground is in truth very hard to protect.

sentences.zh: 兵人散居，無所依恃。

translations.literal: Soldiers living scattered have nothing to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: With troops scattered in separate settlements, there is nothing to depend on.

sentences.zh: 脫有妖姦，必致狼狽。

translations.literal: If evil or treachery should arise, it will necessarily lead to panic and disarray.
translations.idiomatic: Should treachery or sudden trouble appear, the result would surely be panic and rout.

sentences.zh: 雖欲自固，無以得全。

translations.literal: Even if one wishes to secure oneself, there is no way to preserve complete safety.
translations.idiomatic: Even if we tried to hold our position, we could not keep ourselves intact.

sentences.zh: 今求造城儲穀，置兵備守。

translations.literal: Now I ask to build a fort, store grain, and deploy troops for defense.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore ask permission to build a fort, store grain there, and station troops to guard it.

sentences.zh: 鎮自建立，更不煩官。

translations.literal: The garrison will establish it itself and need no further trouble from the officials.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison will raise it on its own and will not burden the central administration further.

sentences.zh: 又於三時之隙，不令廢農。

translations.literal: Also during the intervals of the three farming seasons, farming will not be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Work will be scheduled in the gaps between the three farming seasons so that agriculture is not neglected.

sentences.zh: 一歲、二歲不訖，三歲必成。

translations.literal: If it is not finished in one year or two years, in three years it will certainly be completed.
translations.idiomatic: If it is not finished in one or two years, it will certainly be completed in three.

sentences.zh: 立城之所，必在水陸之次。

translations.literal: The place to establish the fort must be beside both water and land routes.
translations.idiomatic: The site chosen for the fort must lie where water and land routes meet.

sentences.zh: 大小高下，量力取辦。

translations.literal: As to size, height, and scope, take what can be accomplished according to capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Its scale, height, and dimensions should be determined according to what our strength can manage.

sentences.zh: 」詔許之。

translations.literal: " An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved the request.

sentences.zh: 至十年三月，城訖。

translations.literal: By the third month of the tenth year, the fort was completed.
translations.idiomatic: By the third month of the tenth year the fort was finished.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「卿深思遠慮，憂勤盡思，知城已周訖，邊境無不虞之憂，千載有永安之固，朕甚嘉焉。

translations.literal: An edict said: "You think deeply and plan far ahead, anxious and diligent with utmost thought. Knowing the fort is fully completed, the frontier will have no fear of the unforeseen, and for a thousand generations there will be lasting security. I greatly commend this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "You have thought deeply and planned far ahead, laboring with anxious diligence. Now that the fort is fully completed, the frontier will be free of unforeseen danger, and lasting security will endure for ages to come. I greatly commend your achievement.

sentences.zh: 即名此城為刁公城，以旌爾功也。」

translations.literal: Let this fort at once be named Diao Gong Fort to honor your merit."
translations.idiomatic: Let this fort henceforth be named Lord Diao's Fort, to honor your service."

sentences.zh: 興光二年，詔雍還都，拜特進，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xingguang, an edict summoned Yong back to the capital, invested him as Special Advance, and his generalship remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xingguang an edict recalled Yong to the capital, appointed him Special Advance, and left his generalship unchanged.

sentences.zh: 和平六年，表曰：

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Heping, he submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Heping he submitted another memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞有國有家者，莫不禮樂為先。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that those who possess a state or a clan take none before rites and music.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that every lord of a state or head of a clan puts rites and music first.

sentences.zh: 故樂記云：禮所以制外，樂所以修內。

translations.literal: Thus the Record of Music says: Rites are that by which the outer is regulated; music is that by which the inner is cultivated.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Music says: rites govern what is outward; music cultivates what is inward.

sentences.zh: 和氣中釋，恭敬溫文。

translations.literal: Harmonious qi is released within; reverence, respect, warmth, and refinement.
translations.idiomatic: Harmony spreads inward, and reverence, gentleness, and refinement follow.

sentences.zh: 是以安上治民，莫善於禮；

translations.literal: Therefore for securing superiors and governing the people, nothing is better than rites;
translations.idiomatic: Thus for securing those above and governing the people, nothing surpasses rites;

sentences.zh: 易俗移風，莫善於樂。

translations.literal: for changing customs and shifting mores, nothing is better than music.
translations.idiomatic: and for changing customs and transforming the spirit of the age, nothing surpasses music.

sentences.zh: 且於一民一俗，尚須崇而用之，況統御八方，陶鈞六合者哉？

translations.literal: Even for one people and one custom one still must honor and employ them—how much more for one who governs the eight directions and shapes the six quarters?
translations.idiomatic: Even for a single people and a single custom they must still be honored and put to use—how much more for one who rules the eight directions and molds all within the four seas?

sentences.zh: 故帝堯修五禮以明典章，作咸池以諧萬類，顯皇軌於云岱，揚鴻化於介丘。

translations.literal: Therefore Emperor Yao perfected the five rites to clarify statutes and regulations, composed the Xianchi music to harmonize the myriad beings, displayed the imperial track upon Cloud Mount, and spread great transformation west of Mount Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yao therefore perfected the five rites to clarify the canon of governance, composed the Xianchi music to harmonize the myriad creatures, displayed the imperial Way upon Cloud Mount, and spread his great transforming influence from Mount Jie.

sentences.zh: 令木石革心，鳥獸率舞。

translations.literal: He made trees and stones change their hearts, and birds and beasts led one another in dance.
translations.idiomatic: He moved trees and stones to change their hearts, and made birds and beasts dance in unison.

sentences.zh: 包天地之情，達神明之德。

translations.literal: Encompassing the sentiments of Heaven and Earth, reaching the virtue of the spirits and gods.
translations.idiomatic: He embraced the feelings of Heaven and Earth and attained to the virtue of the spirits.

sentences.zh: 夫感天動神，莫近於禮樂。

translations.literal: Of moving Heaven and stirring the spirits, nothing comes closer than rites and music.
translations.idiomatic: Of all things that move Heaven and stir the spirits, none comes nearer than rites and music.

sentences.zh: 故大樂與天地同和，大禮與天地同節。

translations.literal: Therefore great music shares harmony with Heaven and Earth; great rites share measure with Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Great music shares harmony with Heaven and Earth; great rites share measure with Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 和，故百物阜生；

translations.literal: By harmony, therefore the hundred things flourish and live;
translations.idiomatic: Through harmony the hundred things flourish;

sentences.zh: 節，故報天祭地。

translations.literal: by measure, therefore one repays Heaven and sacrifices to Earth.
translations.idiomatic: through measure Heaven is answered and Earth is sacrificed to.

sentences.zh: 禮行於郊，則上下和肅。

translations.literal: When rites are performed in the suburbs, then superiors and inferiors are harmonious and solemn.
translations.idiomatic: When rites are performed in the suburbs, superiors and inferiors become harmonious and solemn.

sentences.zh: 肅者，禮之情；

translations.literal: Solemnity is the sentiment of rites;
translations.idiomatic: Solemnity is the inner quality of rites;

sentences.zh: 和者，樂之致。

translations.literal: harmony is the ultimate attainment of music.
translations.idiomatic: harmony is the highest fulfillment of music.

sentences.zh: 樂至則無怨，禮至則不違。

translations.literal: When music reaches its fullness there is no resentment; when rites reach their fullness there is no transgression.
translations.idiomatic: When music reaches its fullness there is no resentment; when rites reach their fullness there is no violation.

sentences.zh: 揖讓而治天下者，禮樂之謂歟？

translations.literal: Is governing the realm through yielding and deference not what rites and music are called?
translations.idiomatic: Is not the governance of the realm through yielding and deference precisely what rites and music mean?

sentences.zh: 唯聖人知禮樂之不可以已，故作樂以應天，制禮以配地。

translations.literal: Only the sage knows that rites and music cannot be stopped; therefore he makes music to respond to Heaven and institutes rites to match Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Only the sage knows that rites and music must never cease; therefore he composes music to answer Heaven and establishes rites to match Earth.

sentences.zh: 所以承天之道，治人之情。

translations.literal: By this he undertakes Heaven's Way and governs human sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: By this he carries out Heaven's Way and governs human feeling.

sentences.zh: 故王者治定制禮，功成作樂。

translations.literal: Therefore when the king has settled governance he fixes rites; when merit is achieved he composes music.
translations.idiomatic: When a king's rule is settled he fixes the rites; when his achievement is complete he composes music.

sentences.zh: 虞夏殷周，易代而起。

translations.literal: Yu, Xia, Yin, and Zhou rose one after another, replacing dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: The houses of Yu, Xia, Yin, and Zhou rose in succession, each replacing the last.

sentences.zh: 及周之末，王政陵遲。

translations.literal: By the end of Zhou, royal governance declined.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Zhou royal governance had fallen into decay.

sentences.zh: 仲尼傷禮樂之崩亡，痛文武之將墜，自衞返魯，各得其中。

translations.literal: Confucius grieved the collapse and loss of rites and music, lamented that Wen and Wu were about to fall, returned from Wei to Lu, and restored each to its proper mean.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius mourned the collapse of rites and music and grieved that the legacy of Kings Wen and Wu was about to perish; returning from Wei to Lu, he restored each to its proper balance.

sentences.zh: 逮乎秦皇，翦棄道術，灰滅典籍，坑燼儒士，盲天下之目，絕象魏之章，簫韶來儀，不可復矣。

translations.literal: By the time of Qin Shihuang, he cut away and discarded the Way and its arts, reduced the classics to ash, buried and burned the scholars, blinded the eyes of all under Heaven, severed the proclamations of the Elephant Towers, and the Xiaoshao music and coming of the phoenix could never be restored.
translations.idiomatic: By the time of the First Emperor of Qin, the Way and its arts had been cut down and cast aside, the classics burned to ash, and the scholars buried alive; the eyes of the realm were blinded, the proclamations of the Elephant Towers were silenced, and the Xiaoshao music with the coming of the phoenix could never be restored.

sentences.zh: 賴大漢之興，改正朔，易服色，協音樂，制禮儀，正聲古禮，粗欲周備。

translations.literal: Thanks to the rise of Great Han, it corrected the calendar, changed robe colors, harmonized music, established ritual observances, and set right ancient music and ancient rites, roughly seeking completeness.
translations.idiomatic: Only with the rise of Great Han were the calendar corrected, robe colors changed, music harmonized, ritual observances established, and the ancient music and ancient rites set right, so that the system was roughly brought to completion.

sentences.zh: 至於孝章，每以三代損益，優劣殊軌，歎其薄德，無以易民視聽。

translations.literal: Down to Emperor Zhang of Han, each time because the Three Dynasties' additions and subtractions differed in quality and excellence and followed different tracks, he sighed at its meager virtue and had no means to change the people's sight and hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Down to Emperor Zhang of Han, because the additions and subtractions of the Three Dynasties differed in quality and followed separate paths, he sighed at the dynasty's limited virtue and found no way to transform what the people saw and heard.

sentences.zh: 博士曹褒覩斯詔也，知上有制作之意，乃上疏求定諸儀，以為漢禮。

translations.literal: Erudite Cao Bao, seeing this edict, knew the sovereign above had the intent to create and establish, and thereupon submitted a memorial requesting to fix all observances to serve as Han rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Erudite Cao Bao saw this edict, he understood that the throne intended to create new institutions, and submitted a memorial asking to fix all observances as the rites of Han.

sentences.zh: 終於休廢，寢而不行。

translations.literal: In the end it rested and was abandoned, left to sleep and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the project was shelved and never carried out.

sentences.zh: 及魏晉之日，修而不備。

translations.literal: By the days of Wei and Jin, they were revised but not complete.
translations.idiomatic: By the time of Wei and Jin the rites were revised but still incomplete.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下無為以恭己，使賢以御世，方鳴和鸞以陟岱宗，陪羣后以昇中岳，而三禮闕於唐辰，象舞替於周日。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty governs through nonaction and honors himself with reverence, employs the worthy to govern the age, and is just about to sound harmonious bells and ascend Mount Tai, accompany the feudal lords in ascending the Central Peak—yet the three rites are lacking from the time of Tang, and the elephant dance has been replaced since the Zhou days.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that Your Majesty governs through nonaction and reverent self-restraint, employs the worthy to rule the age, and is on the verge of sounding harmonious bells to ascend Mount Tai and accompanying the feudal lords to the Central Peak—yet the three rites have been absent since the age of Tang, and the elephant dance has fallen away since the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 夫君舉必書，古之典也。

translations.literal: For a ruler's actions must be recorded—this is the ancient canon.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler's every act must be recorded—such is the ancient canon.

sentences.zh: 柴望之禮，帝王盛事。

translations.literal: The rites of faggot and lookout are the great affairs of emperors and kings.
translations.idiomatic: The rites of faggot and lookout are the supreme ceremonies of emperors and kings.

sentences.zh: 臣今以為有其時而無其禮，有其德而無其樂。

translations.literal: Your subject now considers that there is the proper time but not the proper rites, and there is the virtue but not the music.
translations.idiomatic: I now believe that the time is at hand but the rites are lacking, and the virtue is present but the music is not.

sentences.zh: 史闕封石之文，工絕清頌之饗，良由禮樂不興，王政有闕所致也。

translations.literal: Histories lack the texts of the sealed stone, craftsmen have ceased the pure sacrificial feasts of song-praise—truly because rites and music do not flourish and royal governance has lacunae, that which is caused thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Historical records lack the sealing-stone inscriptions, and craftsmen have abandoned the pure sacrificial hymns—truly because rites and music have not been revived and royal governance has gaps, as that which is caused thereby.

sentences.zh: [5]臣聞樂由禮，所以象德；

translations.literal: [5] Your subject has heard that music derives from rites, by which virtue is imaged;
translations.idiomatic: [5] I have heard that music arises from rites and thereby images virtue;

sentences.zh: 禮由樂，所以防淫。

translations.literal: rites derive from music, by which excess is prevented.
translations.idiomatic: and rites arise from music and thereby guard against excess.

sentences.zh: 五帝殊時不相沿，三王異世不相襲。

translations.literal: The Five Emperors in different times did not follow one another; the Three Kings in different generations did not inherit from one another.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Emperors lived in different ages and did not simply follow one another; the Three Kings ruled in different generations and did not merely inherit from their predecessors.

sentences.zh: 事與時並，名與功偕故也。

translations.literal: Affairs match the times, and names accompany achievements—this is why.
translations.idiomatic: Affairs must accord with the times, and names must match achievements—this is why.

sentences.zh: 臣識昧儒先，管窺不遠，謂宜修禮正樂，以光大聖之治。

translations.literal: Your subject's knowledge is dim before the Confucian ancients, and peering through a bamboo tube I cannot see far; I say rites should be revised and music rectified to amplify and brighten the sage's governance.
translations.idiomatic: My learning is dim before the Confucian ancients, and what I see through a bamboo tube does not reach far; yet I hold that rites should be restored and music rectified to enlarge and illuminate the sage ruler's governance.

sentences.zh: 詔令公卿集議，會高宗崩，遂寢。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the high ministers to assemble for deliberation; when Emperor Wencheng died, the matter then lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the high ministers to meet and deliberate, but when Emperor Wencheng died the proposal was shelved.

sentences.zh: 皇興中，雍與隴西王源賀及中書監高允等並以耆年特見優禮，錫雍几杖，劍履上殿，月致珍羞焉。

translations.literal: During Huangxing, Yong together with Wang Yuanhe of Longxi and Chief Secretary Supervisor Gao Yun and others were all specially honored because of their great age; Yong was granted an armrest and staff, allowed to ascend the hall with sword and shoes, and delicacies were sent to him each month.
translations.idiomatic: During Huangxing, Yong, together with Wang Yuanhe of Longxi and Chief Secretary Supervisor Gao Yun and others, received special honors on account of their great age. Yong was granted an armrest and staff, permitted to enter the hall bearing sword and wearing shoes, and sent delicacies every month.

sentences.zh: 雍性寬柔，好尚文典，手不釋書，明敏多智。

translations.literal: Yong's character was broad and gentle; he loved and honored literary classics, never releasing a book from his hand; he was clear-minded, quick, and richly intelligent.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was broad-minded and gentle by nature. He loved the literary classics and never let a book leave his hand; he was clear-minded, quick-witted, and deeply intelligent.

sentences.zh: 凡所為詩賦頌論并雜文，百有餘篇。

translations.literal: All the poems, rhapsodies, eulogies, treatises, and miscellaneous writings he composed numbered more than a hundred pieces.
translations.idiomatic: All the poems, rhapsodies, eulogies, essays, and miscellaneous pieces he wrote numbered more than a hundred.

sentences.zh: 又汎施愛士，怡靜寡欲。

translations.literal: He also spread affection broadly and loved scholars; serene and quiet, with few desires.
translations.idiomatic: He was generous in affection toward scholars, serene and quiet, and little given to desire.

sentences.zh: 篤信佛道，著教誡二十餘篇，以訓導子孫。

translations.literal: He devoutly believed in the Buddhist Way, composed more than twenty chapters of instruction and admonition to train and guide his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: He devoutly believed in the Buddhist Way and wrote more than twenty chapters of instruction and admonition to guide his descendants.

sentences.zh: 太和八年冬卒，年九十五。

translations.literal: In the winter of the eighth year of Taihe he died, aged ninety-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the eighth year of Taihe he died at the age of ninety-five.

sentences.zh: 賜命服一襲，賵帛五百匹，贈儀同三司、冀州刺史，將軍如故，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: He was granted one suit of life-robes, five hundred bolts of burial silk, posthumously honored as Grand Master of Splendid Honors and Inspector of Ji province, his generalship remaining as before, and given the posthumous title Simple.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted one suit of court robes, five hundred bolts of burial silk, and posthumously honored as Grand Master of Splendid Honors and Inspector of Ji province while retaining his former generalship; his posthumous title was Simple.

sentences.zh: 雍長子纂，字奉宗。

translations.literal: Yong's eldest son Zuan, styled Fengzong.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's eldest son was Zuan, whose courtesy name was Fengzong.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: He died early.
translations.idiomatic: He died young.

sentences.zh: 纂弟遵，字奉國。

translations.literal: Zuan's younger brother Zun, styled Fengguo.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan's younger brother was Zun, whose courtesy name was Fengguo.

sentences.zh: 襲爵。

translations.literal: He inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the marquisate.

sentences.zh: 遵弟紹，字奉世。

translations.literal: Zun's younger brother Shao, styled Fengshi.
translations.idiomatic: Zun's younger brother was Shao, whose courtesy name was Fengshi.

sentences.zh: 武騎侍郎、汝陰王天賜涼州征西府司馬。

translations.literal: Gentleman of the Martial Riders, Staff Officer of the Western Campaign Headquarters of Liangzhou under Prince Tianci of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Gentleman of the Martial Riders and as Staff Officer of the Western Campaign Headquarters in Liangzhou under Prince Tianci of Runan.

sentences.zh: 紹弟獻，字奉章。

translations.literal: Shao's younger brother Xian, styled Fengzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's younger brother was Xian, whose courtesy name was Fengzhang.

sentences.zh: 祕書郎。

translations.literal: Secretariat Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Secretariat Clerk.

sentences.zh: 獻弟融，字奉業。

translations.literal: Xian's younger brother Rong, styled Fengye.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's younger brother was Rong, whose courtesy name was Fengye.

sentences.zh: 汝陰太守。

translations.literal: Administrator of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Administrator of Runan.

sentences.zh: 融弟肅，字奉誠。

translations.literal: Rong's younger brother Su, styled Fengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's younger brother was Su, whose courtesy name was Fengcheng.

sentences.zh: 中書博士。

translations.literal: Secretariat Erudite.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Secretariat Erudite.

sentences.zh: 遵少不拘小節，長更修改。

translations.literal: Zun in youth did not constrain himself in small matters; grown, he changed and corrected himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zun in youth paid little heed to small proprieties, but as he grew older he reformed himself.

sentences.zh: 太和中，例降為侯。

translations.literal: During Taihe, by precedent his rank was reduced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: During Taihe, by precedent his title was reduced to marquis.

sentences.zh: [6]景明中，除相州魏郡太守。

translations.literal: [6] During Jingming, he was appointed Administrator of Wei Commandery in Xiang province.
translations.idiomatic: [6] During Jingming he was appointed Administrator of Wei Commandery in Xiang province.

sentences.zh: 還為太尉諮議參軍。

translations.literal: On return he became Consultation Officer on the staff of the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he became Consultation Officer on the staff of the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 年七十，志力不衰。

translations.literal: At seventy years, his will and strength did not wane.
translations.idiomatic: At seventy his resolve and vigor had not declined.

sentences.zh: 嘗經篤疾，幾死，見神明救免，言是福門之子，當享長年。

translations.literal: Once he suffered grave illness and nearly died; he saw spirits and gods rescue and spare him, saying he was a son of the Gate of Fortune and would enjoy long years.
translations.idiomatic: Once he fell gravely ill and nearly died; he saw spirits intervene to save him, declaring that he was a son of the Gate of Fortune and would enjoy long life.

sentences.zh: 延昌三年，遷司農少卿。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yanchang, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yanchang he was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 尋拜龍驤將軍、洛州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed General of the Flying Dragon and Inspector of Luo province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed General of the Flying Dragon and Inspector of Luo province.

sentences.zh: 遵招誘有方，蕭衍新化太守杜性、新化令杜龍振、平陽令杜臺定等，率戶三千據地內附。

translations.literal: Zun had effective methods of attraction; Du Xing, Administrator of Xinhua under Xiao Yan, Du Longzhen, Magistrate of Xinhua, Du Taiding, Magistrate of Pingyang, and others led three thousand households in occupying territory and submitting inward allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Zun had effective methods of winning people over. Du Xing, Administrator of Xinhua under Xiao Yan, together with Du Longzhen, Magistrate of Xinhua, Du Taiding, Magistrate of Pingyang, and others led three thousand households in occupying territory and submitting to Wei.

sentences.zh: 熙平元年七月卒，年七十六。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Xiping he died, aged seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first year of Xiping he died at the age of seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 贈平東將軍、兗州刺史，諡曰惠侯。

translations.literal: He was posthumously honored as General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Yan province, with the posthumous title Marquis of Kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Yan province, with the posthumous title Marquis Kind.

sentences.zh: 有子十三人。

translations.literal: He had thirteen sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had thirteen sons.

sentences.zh: 長子楷，字景伯。

translations.literal: His eldest son Kai, styled Jingbo.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son was Kai, whose courtesy name was Jingbo.

sentences.zh: 州舉秀才。

translations.literal: The province recommended him as Filial-Piety and Incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: He was recommended as Filial-Piety and Incorrupt by his province.

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: He died early.
translations.idiomatic: He died young.

sentences.zh: 子沖，字文助。

translations.literal: His son Chong, styled Wenzhu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Chong, whose courtesy name was Wenzhu.

sentences.zh: [7]在儒林傳。

translations.literal: [7] He is in the Biographies of Confucian Scholars.
translations.idiomatic: [7] His biography appears in the Biographies of Confucian Scholars.

sentences.zh: 楷弟尚，字景勝。

translations.literal: Kai's younger brother Shang, styled Jingsheng.
translations.idiomatic: Kai's younger brother was Shang, whose courtesy name was Jingsheng.

sentences.zh: 本州治中。

translations.literal: Provincial Aide of his native province.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Provincial Aide in his home province.

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: He died early.
translations.idiomatic: He died young.

sentences.zh: 尚弟整，字景智。

translations.literal: Shang's younger brother Zheng, styled Jingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Shang's younger brother was Zheng, whose courtesy name was Jingzhi.

sentences.zh: 少有大度，頗涉書史。

translations.literal: From youth he had great magnanimity and broadly entered into books and histories.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was broad-minded and well read in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 郡功曹。

translations.literal: Commandery Merit Officer.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Merit Officer of his commandery.

sentences.zh: 太和十五年，奉朝請。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Taihe, he was made Attendant at Court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Taihe he was appointed Attendant at Court.

sentences.zh: 高祖都洛，親自臨選，除司空法曹參軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen established the capital at Luoyang, he personally attended the selection and appointed Zheng Assistant in the Legal Bureau of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen moved the capital to Luoyang and personally oversaw the selection of officials, Zheng was appointed Assistant in the Legal Bureau of the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 高祖南討，以廣陽王嘉鎮荊州，整為嘉外兵參軍事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen campaigned south, he had Prince of Guangyang Jia garrison Jing province, and Zheng served as Outside Troops Staff Officer on Jia's staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen marched south, Prince of Guangyang Jia was posted to garrison Jing province, and Zheng served on his staff as Outside Troops Staff Officer.

sentences.zh: 尋轉太尉、咸陽王禧外兵參軍。

translations.literal: Soon after he was transferred to Outside Troops Staff Officer on the staff of the Grand Commandant and Prince of Xianyang Xi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Outside Troops Staff Officer on the staff of the Grand Commandant and Prince of Xianyang Xi.

sentences.zh: 景明中，除給事中，領本州中正。

translations.literal: During Jingming he was appointed Supervising Censor and concurrently served as Chief Rectifier of his native province.
translations.idiomatic: During Jingming he was appointed Supervising Censor and concurrently served as Chief Rectifier of his home province.

sentences.zh: 尋除尚書左中兵郎中。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed Left Central Troops Master of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed Left Central Troops Master of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 正始中，蕭衍江州刺史王茂先來寇南境，平南將軍楊大眼討之，詔整持節為大眼軍司，大破茂先，斬衍輔國將軍王花等。

translations.literal: During Zhengshi, Xiao Yan's Jiangzhou Inspector Wang Mao came first to raid the southern frontier; General Who Pacifies the South Yang Dayan attacked him. An edict made Zheng Bearer of the Staff and Army Aide to Dayan. He routed Mao's forces and beheaded Xiao Yan's General Who Assists the State Wang Hua and others.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhengshi, Wang Mao, Jiangzhou inspector under Xiao Yan, launched an early raid on the southern frontier. General Who Pacifies the South Yang Dayan was sent against him, and an edict appointed Zheng Bearer of the Staff as Dayan's army aide. Zheng won a great victory over Mao and beheaded Xiao Yan's General Who Assists the State Wang Hua and others.

sentences.zh: 永平初，以軍功除員外散騎常侍，仍除郎中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongping, for military merit he was appointed Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and was again appointed Master of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yongping he was appointed Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry for his military achievements, while retaining his post as Master of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 延昌三年秋，世宗親選百官於朝堂，拜右軍將軍，仍除郎中。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the third year of Yanchang, Emperor Xuanwu personally selected the hundred officials in the Hall of Court, appointed Zheng General of the Right Army, and again made him Master of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the third year of Yanchang, Emperor Xuanwu personally selected officials in the Hall of Court, appointed Zheng General of the Right Army, and again retained him as Master of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 尋轉驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: Soon after he was transferred to General of the Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to General of the Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 未幾，丁父憂。

translations.literal: Before long he entered mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he entered mourning upon his father's death.

sentences.zh: 相州刺史、中山王熙在鄴起兵，[8]將誅元叉等。

translations.literal: Xiang province Inspector and Prince of Zhongshan Xi raised troops at Ye [8] intending to execute Yuan Cha and others.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xi, Prince of Zhongshan and inspector of Xiang province, raised troops at Ye [8] intending to execute Yuan Cha and his faction.

sentences.zh: 事敗，傳首京師，熙之親故莫敢視。

translations.literal: The affair failed; his head was sent to the capital, and Xi's kin and old associates did not dare to look upon it.
translations.idiomatic: When the revolt failed, Xi's head was sent to the capital, and none of his kin or old associates dared look upon it.

sentences.zh: 整弟婦即熙姊，遂收其屍藏之，後乃還熙所親。

translations.literal: Zheng's younger brother's wife was Xi's elder sister, so she took in his corpse and hid it, afterward returning it to Xi's kin.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's sister-in-law was Xi's elder sister. She recovered his body and hid it, then later returned it to Xi's family.

sentences.zh: 叉聞而致憾，因以熙弟略南走蕭衍，誣整將叛，送整與弟宣及子恭等幽繫之。

translations.literal: Cha heard of this and bore resentment; citing Xi's younger brother Lue's flight south to Xiao Yan, he falsely accused Zheng of plotting rebellion and had Zheng, his younger brother Xuan, his son Gong, and others imprisoned in secret.
translations.idiomatic: When Cha heard of this he nursed a grudge. Citing the flight of Xi's younger brother Lue to Xiao Yan in the south, he falsely accused Zheng of plotting rebellion and had Zheng, his brother Xuan, his son Gong, and others secretly imprisoned.

sentences.zh: [9]賴御史王基、前軍將檢事使魏子建理雪，獲免。

translations.literal: [9] Relying on Censor Wang Ji and Forward Army General and Investigating Commissioner Wei Zijian to clear the case, he obtained release.
translations.idiomatic: [9] Thanks to Censor Wang Ji and Forward Army General and Investigating Commissioner Wei Zijian, who cleared his name, he was released.

sentences.zh: 後自征虜將軍出除范陽太守。

translations.literal: Later, from the post of General Who Campaigns Against Barbarians he went out and was appointed Administrator of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later he left the capital from his post as General Who Campaigns Against Barbarians to become Administrator of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 時已兵亂，整郡獲全。

translations.literal: At that time warfare had already broken out, yet Zheng's commandery remained intact.
translations.idiomatic: By then the realm was already torn by war, yet under Zheng the commandery remained intact.

sentences.zh: 去郡之後，尋被陷沒。

translations.literal: After he left the commandery, it was soon overrun and lost.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he left the post, the commandery fell.

sentences.zh: 靈太后反政，除安南將軍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling restored her rule, he was appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling regained power, he was appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 元略曾於整坐泣謂黃門王誦、尚書袁翻曰：「刁公收斂我家，卿等宜知。」

translations.literal: Yuan Lue once wept at Zheng's seat and said to Yellow Gate Wang Song and Secretary Yuan Fan: "Master Diao has seized and shut up my household—you ought to know this."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Lue once wept in Zheng's presence and said to Wang Song of the Yellow Gate and Secretary Yuan Fan, "Master Diao has stripped my household bare. You ought to know this."

sentences.zh: 整以母老，河北喪亂，時整族弟雙為西兗州刺史，整遂攜家依焉。

translations.literal: Because Zheng's mother was old and Hebei was ravaged by war, and at that time Zheng's clansman younger cousin Shuang was Inspector of Western Yan province, Zheng thereupon took his household and relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's mother was elderly, and Hebei was in turmoil. His clansman Shuang was then inspector of Western Yan province, so Zheng moved his household to join him.

sentences.zh: 永安初，拜金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yong'an, he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Purple Seal.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yong'an he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Purple Seal.

sentences.zh: 二年，兼黃門。

translations.literal: In the second year he concurrently served in the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he also served in the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，用為滄州刺史。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Zheng was employed as Inspector of Cang province.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Zheng was appointed Inspector of Cang province.

sentences.zh: 莊帝還朝，坐免官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangdi returned to court, Zheng was dismissed from office for his involvement.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuangdi returned to the throne, Zheng was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 後歸鄉里。

translations.literal: Later he returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: He later returned to his home district.

sentences.zh: 及莊帝殺尒朱榮，就除鎮東將軍、行滄州事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangdi killed Erzhu Rong, Zheng was immediately appointed General Who Guards the East and Acting Administrator of Cang province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuangdi killed Erzhu Rong, Zheng was immediately appointed General Who Guards the East with authority over Cang province.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，假征東大將軍、滄冀瀛三州刺史、大都督，將軍如前。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Putai, he was provisionally made General Who Campaigns East, Inspector of Cang, Ji, and Ying provinces, and Commander-in-Chief; his generalship remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Putai he was provisionally appointed General Who Campaigns East, Inspector of Cang, Ji, and Ying, and Commander-in-Chief, while retaining his previous rank as general.

sentences.zh: 尋加車騎將軍、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Soon after he was further made General of Chariots and Cavalry and Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon further promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry and Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 逢本鄉賊亂，奉母客於齊州。

translations.literal: When bandit turmoil broke out in his home district, he escorted his mother as a guest to Qi province.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits ravaged his home district, he took his mother to stay as a guest in Qi province.

sentences.zh: 加衞大將軍。

translations.literal: He was further made Grand General of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to Grand General of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 天平四年，卒於鄴。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianping he died at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianping he died at Ye.

sentences.zh: 贈司空公，諡曰文獻。

translations.literal: He was posthumously honored as Duke of the Minister of Works, with the posthumous title Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Duke of the Minister of Works, with the posthumous title Cultured and Meritorious.

sentences.zh: 整解音律，輕財好施，交結名勝，聲酒自娛。

translations.literal: Zheng understood musical pitch and temperament, treated wealth lightly and loved giving, formed ties with celebrated figures, and amused himself with music and wine.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng understood music, was generous with his wealth, sought out celebrated company, and took his pleasure in song and wine.

sentences.zh: 然貪而好色，為議者所貶。

translations.literal: Yet he was greedy and fond of women, and was disparaged by those who commented on such matters.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was greedy and fond of women, and critics spoke ill of him for it.

sentences.zh: 初雍與從弟寶惠俱入國。

translations.literal: At first Yong and his younger cousin Bao Hui both entered the state together.
translations.idiomatic: In the beginning Yong and his younger cousin Bao Hui had entered Wei together.

sentences.zh: 寶惠，字道明，太祖以為上客。

translations.literal: Bao Hui, styled Daoming, was made a Distinguished Guest by Emperor Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Hui, whose courtesy name was Daoming, was treated by Emperor Taizu as a distinguished guest.

sentences.zh: 卒，有六子。

translations.literal: When he died he had six sons.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he left six sons.

sentences.zh: 子連城，為冀州開府掾。

translations.literal: His son Liancheng served as Aide of the General Who Opens a Commandery in Ji province.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liancheng served as staff aide to the general who opened a commandery in Ji province.

sentences.zh: 刁氏世有榮祿，而門風不甚修潔，為時所鄙。

translations.literal: The Diao clan for generations enjoyed honor and stipend, yet its household conduct was not very refined and pure, and it was despised by the age.
translations.idiomatic: The Diao clan had enjoyed rank and emolument for generations, yet its household conduct was not especially upright, and contemporaries looked down on it.

sentences.zh: 雍族孫雙，字子山。

translations.literal: Yong's clansman grandson Shuang, styled Zishan.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's clansman Shuang, whose courtesy name was Zishan.

sentences.zh: 高祖藪，晉齊郡太守。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Sou was Jin Administrator of Qi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Sou had served Jin as Administrator of Qi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 藪因晉亂居青州之樂安。

translations.literal: Because of Jin disorder Sou dwelt at Le'an in Qing province.
translations.idiomatic: During the chaos of Jin, Sou settled at Le'an in Qing province.

sentences.zh: 父道履，皇興初，除平原太守。

translations.literal: His father Daolu, at the beginning of Huangxing, was appointed Administrator of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Daolu was appointed Administrator of Pingyuan at the beginning of Huangxing.

sentences.zh: 至雙始還本鄉。

translations.literal: Only when Shuang came did the family return to its native district.
translations.idiomatic: It was only in Shuang's time that the family returned to its native district.

sentences.zh: 雙少好學，兼涉文史，雅為中山王英所知賞。

translations.literal: Shuang from youth loved learning and also entered into literature and history; he was properly known and appreciated by Prince of Zhongshan Ying.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Shuang loved learning and was well versed in literature and history. Prince of Zhongshan Ying held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 拜西河太守。

translations.literal: He was appointed Administrator of Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Administrator of Xihe.

sentences.zh: 正光初，中山王熙之誅也，熙弟略投命於雙，雙護之周年。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengguang, when Prince of Zhongshan Xi was executed, Xi's younger brother Lue entrusted his life to Shuang, and Shuang protected him for a full year.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhengguang, after Prince of Zhongshan Xi was executed, Xi's younger brother Lue placed himself in Shuang's care, and Shuang sheltered him for a full year.

sentences.zh: 時購略甚切。

translations.literal: At that time the hunt for Lue was very urgent.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the hunt for Lue was fierce.

sentences.zh: 略乃謂雙曰：「我兄弟屠滅已盡，唯我一身漏刃相託。

translations.literal: Lue then said to Shuang: "My brothers have been slaughtered to the last man; I alone escaped the blade and entrust myself to you.
translations.idiomatic: Lue then said to Shuang, "My brothers have been slaughtered to the last man. I alone slipped through the blade and now entrust myself to you.

sentences.zh: 卿雖厚恩，久見容蔽，但事留變生，終恐難保。

translations.literal: Although you have shown great kindness and long concealed me, yet if the matter lingers change will arise, and in the end I fear it will be hard to preserve.
translations.idiomatic: You have shown me great kindness and sheltered me for a long time, but if this drags on, circumstances will change and I fear you will not be able to protect me forever.

sentences.zh: 脫萬一發覺，我死分也，無事相累卿。

translations.literal: If by any chance I am discovered, my death is my allotted portion; there is no reason to involve you.
translations.idiomatic: If I am discovered, my death is my own fate. There is no need for you to be dragged down with me.

sentences.zh: 若送吾出境，便是再生之惠，如其不爾，輒欲自裁。

translations.literal: If you send me beyond the border, that will be the grace of renewed life; if not, I mean at once to take my own life.
translations.idiomatic: If you send me across the border, that will be a debt of life renewed. Otherwise I mean to take my own life at once.

sentences.zh: 」雙曰：「人生會有一死，死所難遇耳。

translations.literal: " Shuang said: "In life one must meet death once; a death worth meeting is hard to encounter.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang replied, "Every man must die once. What is hard is to meet a death worth dying.

sentences.zh: 今遭知己，視死如歸，願不以為慮。

translations.literal: Now having met one who knows me, I regard death as returning home; I wish you not to take this as a worry.
translations.idiomatic: Now that I have found a true friend, I look on death as going home. Please do not worry on my account.

sentences.zh: 」略後苦求南轉，雙乃遣從子昌送達江左。

translations.literal: " Later Lue urgently begged to go south; Shuang then sent his nephew Chang to escort him and deliver him to the lands east of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Later Lue pressed hard to go south. Shuang then sent his nephew Chang to escort him safely to the lands east of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 靈太后返政，知略因雙獲免，徵拜光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling restored her rule, knowing that Lue had escaped through Shuang, she summoned and appointed Shuang Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling regained power and learned that Lue had escaped through Shuang's help, she summoned Shuang and appointed him Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 時略姊饒安公主，刁宣妻也，頻訴靈太后，乞徵略還朝廷。

translations.literal: At that time Lue's elder sister was Princess Rao'an, wife of Diao Xuan; she repeatedly appealed to Empress Dowager Ling, begging that Lue be summoned back to court.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Lue's elder sister was Princess Rao'an, wife of Diao Xuan. She repeatedly appealed to Empress Dowager Ling, asking that Lue be summoned back to court.

sentences.zh: 乃以徐州所獲俘江革、祖暅二人易之。
