translations.literal: Thereupon Jiang Ge and Zu Xuan, two captives taken in Xu province, were exchanged for him.
translations.idiomatic: The court then exchanged him for two captives taken in Xu province, Jiang Ge and Zu Xuan.

sentences.zh: 以雙與略有舊，乃令至境迎接略。

translations.literal: Because Shuang had old ties with Lue, he was ordered to go to the border and receive Lue.
translations.idiomatic: Because Shuang and Lue were old friends, Shuang was ordered to the border to receive him.

sentences.zh: 肅宗末，除西兗州刺史。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Suzong's reign he was appointed Inspector of Western Yan province.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Emperor Suzong's reign he was appointed Inspector of Western Yan province.

sentences.zh: 時賊盜蜂起，州人張桃弓等招聚亡命，公行劫掠。

translations.literal: At that time bandits and robbers swarmed like bees; men of the province such as Zhang Taogong gathered fugitives and openly carried out plunder.
translations.idiomatic: At that time bandits swarmed everywhere. Local men such as Zhang Taogong gathered fugitives and openly plundered the countryside.

sentences.zh: 雙至境，先遣使諭桃弓，陳示禍福，桃弓即隨使歸罪，雙捨而不問。

translations.literal: When Shuang reached the border of his province, he first sent an envoy to instruct Taogong, setting forth fortune and disaster; Taogong at once followed the envoy to submit himself to judgment, and Shuang pardoned him without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuang reached his province, he first sent an envoy to reason with Taogong, explaining the consequences of his course. Taogong at once came with the envoy to surrender, and Shuang pardoned him without punishment.

sentences.zh: 後有盜發之處，令桃弓追捕，咸悉擒獲。

translations.literal: Later, wherever robberies occurred, he ordered Taogong to pursue them, and all were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, whenever robberies occurred, he ordered Taogong to hunt the culprits down, and all were captured.

sentences.zh: 於是州境清肅。

translations.literal: Thereupon the province's territory became clear and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter order was restored throughout the province.

sentences.zh: 莊帝初，行濟州刺史，以功封曲城鄉男。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Zhuangdi's reign he acted as Inspector of Ji province and, for merit, was enfeoffed as Baron of Qucheng Village.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Zhuangdi's reign he served as acting inspector of Ji province and, for his achievements, was enfeoffed as Baron of Qucheng Village.

sentences.zh: 出帝初，遷驃騎大將軍、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Chudi's reign he was transferred to General of the Valiant Cavalry and Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Chudi's reign he was promoted to General of the Valiant Cavalry and Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: [10]興和三年卒。

translations.literal: [10] In the third year of Xinghe he died.
translations.idiomatic: [10] He died in the third year of Xinghe.

sentences.zh: 贈車騎大將軍、儀同三司、齊州刺史，諡曰清穆。

translations.literal: He was posthumously honored as General of Chariots and Cavalry, with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies, and Inspector of Qi province, with the posthumous title Qingmu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as General of Chariots and Cavalry with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies and as Inspector of Qi province, with the posthumous title Pure and Solemn.

sentences.zh: 王慧龍，自云太原晉陽人，司馬德宗尚書僕射愉之孫，散騎侍郎緝之子也。

translations.literal: Wang Huilong declared himself a man of Jinyang in Taiyuan, grandson of Sima Dezong's Vice Director of the Secretariat Yu, and son of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huilong claimed to be a native of Jinyang in Taiyuan. He was the grandson of Yu, Vice Director of the Secretariat under Emperor An of Jin, and the son of Ji, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 幼聰慧，愉以為諸孫之龍，故名焉。

translations.literal: From childhood he was clever and quick; Yu took him to be the dragon among his grandsons, and so named him thus.
translations.idiomatic: As a child he was clever and gifted. Yu took him to be the dragon among his grandsons, and so gave him the name Huilong, "Wise Dragon."

sentences.zh: 初，劉裕微時，愉不為禮，及得志，愉合家見誅。

translations.literal: At first, when Liu Yu was still obscure, Yu did not show him courtesy; when Liu Yu achieved his aim, Yu's whole household was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Liu Yu was still obscure, Yu had treated him without courtesy. When Liu Yu rose to power, Yu's entire household was executed.

sentences.zh: 慧龍年十四，為沙門僧彬所匿。

translations.literal: Huilong was fourteen years old and was hidden by the monk Seng Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Huilong was fourteen and was hidden by the monk Seng Bin.

sentences.zh: 百餘日，將慧龍過江，為津人所疑，曰：「行意怱怱徬徨，得非王氏諸子乎？

translations.literal: After more than a hundred days, as he was taking Huilong across the river, a ferryman grew suspicious and said: "Your manner is hurried and restless—could you not be sons of the Wang clan?"
translations.idiomatic: After more than a hundred days, as he was taking Huilong across the river, a ferryman grew suspicious and said, "You look hurried and restless. Could you be sons of the Wang clan?"

sentences.zh: 」僧彬曰：「貧道從師有年，止西岸，今暫欲定省，還期無遠，此隨吾受業者，何至如君言。

translations.literal: " Seng Bin said: "This poor monk has followed his teacher for years and stays on the west bank; now I briefly wish to visit home, and my return is not far off. This one follows me in study—how could matters be as you say?"
translations.idiomatic: Seng Bin replied, "I have studied under my teacher for years and live on the west bank. I am only going home for a brief visit and will return soon. This boy studies with me. How could things be as you say?"

sentences.zh: 」既濟，遂西上江陵，依叔祖忱故吏荊州前治中習辟疆。

translations.literal: " Once they had crossed, they then went west upriver to Jiangling and relied on Xi's former clerk, former Aide of Jing province Xi Pijiang.
translations.idiomatic: Once they had crossed, they went west to Jiangling and took refuge with Xi Pijiang, a former aide of Jing province and onetime retainer of Huilong's grand-uncle Chen.

sentences.zh: 時刺史魏詠之卒，辟疆與江陵令羅脩、前別駕劉期公、土人王騰等謀舉兵，推慧龍為盟主，剋日襲州城。

translations.literal: At that time Inspector Wei Yongzhi died; Pijiang, together with Jiangling Magistrate Luo Xiu, former Vice Director Liu Qigong, local man Wang Teng, and others plotted to raise troops, making Huilong covenant leader and fixing a day to storm the provincial city.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the inspector Wei Yongzhi died. Pijiang, together with Jiangling magistrate Luo Xiu, former vice director Liu Qigong, the local leader Wang Teng, and others plotted to raise troops, making Huilong their covenant leader and fixing a day to storm the provincial city.

sentences.zh: 而劉裕聞詠之卒，亦懼江陵有變，遣其弟道規為荊州，眾遂不果。

translations.literal: But Liu Yu, hearing of Yongzhi's death, also feared trouble at Jiangling and sent his younger brother Daogui to Jing province, so the crowd's plan did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: But Liu Yu, hearing of Yongzhi's death, feared unrest at Jiangling and sent his younger brother Daogui to take over Jing province, so the plot came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 羅脩將慧龍，又與僧彬北詣襄陽。

translations.literal: Luo Xiu took Huilong and, together with Seng Bin, went north to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Xiu took Huilong and, together with Seng Bin, went north to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 司馬德宗雍州刺史魯宗之資給慧龍，送渡江，遂自虎牢奔于姚興。

translations.literal: Sima Dezong's Yong province Inspector Lu Zongzhi supplied Huilong, sent him across the river, and he then fled from Hulao to Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zongzhi, Yong province inspector under Emperor An of Jin, supplied Huilong and helped him cross the river. Huilong then fled from Hulao to Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 其自言也如此。

translations.literal: His own account was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the account he gave of himself.

sentences.zh: 泰常二年，姚泓滅，慧龍歸國。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taichang, when Yao Hong was destroyed, Huilong returned to the state.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taichang, after Yao Hong's defeat, Huilong returned to Wei.

sentences.zh: 太宗引見與言，慧龍請效力南討，言終，俯而流涕，天子為之動容。

translations.literal: Emperor Mingyuan received him in audience and spoke with him; Huilong asked to devote his strength to the southern campaign. When his words ended he bowed his head and wept, and the Son of Heaven was moved on his account.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingyuan received him in audience. Huilong asked to serve in the southern campaigns, and when he finished speaking he bowed his head and wept. The emperor was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 謂曰：「朕方混一車書，席卷吳會，卿情計如此，豈不能相資以眾乎？

translations.literal: He said to him: "We are now unifying carriage and script and sweeping up Wu and Kuai; with your feelings and plans as they are, can We not support you with troops?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to him, "I am now uniting the realm and sweeping through Wu and Kuai. With devotion such as yours, can I not supply you with an army?"

sentences.zh: 」然亦未之用。

translations.literal: " Yet in the end he was not employed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the end Huilong was not employed.

sentences.zh: 後拜洛城鎮將，配兵三千人鎮金墉。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Garrison General of Luocheng, assigned three thousand troops, and garrisoned Jinyong.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Garrison General of Luocheng, given three thousand troops, and posted to garrison Jinyong.

sentences.zh: 既拜十餘日，太宗崩。

translations.literal: Within more than ten days after his appointment, Emperor Mingyuan died.
translations.idiomatic: Within little more than ten days of his appointment, Emperor Mingyuan died.

sentences.zh: 世祖初即位，咸謂南人不宜委以師旅之任，遂停前授。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taiwu first ascended the throne, all said that southerners ought not be entrusted with command of armies, and so the earlier appointment was halted.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu first ascended the throne, court opinion held that a southerner should not be entrusted with military command, and Huilong's appointment was revoked.

sentences.zh: 初，崔浩弟恬聞慧龍王氏子，以女妻之。

translations.literal: At first, Cui Hao's younger brother Tian, hearing that Huilong was a son of the Wang clan, gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Cui Hao's younger brother Tian, hearing that Huilong was a son of the Wang clan, gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 浩既婚姻，及見慧龍，曰：「信王家兒也。

translations.literal: After Hao had formed the marriage tie and saw Huilong, he said: "Truly a son of the Wang house.
translations.idiomatic: Once the marriage tie was formed and Hao saw Huilong, he said, "He is truly a son of the Wang house.

sentences.zh: 」王氏世齇鼻，江東謂之齇王。

translations.literal: " The Wang clan for generations had snub noses; east of the Yangzi they were called the Snub-Nose Wangs.
translations.idiomatic: The Wang clan for generations had snub noses. East of the Yangzi they were called the Snub-Nose Wangs.

sentences.zh: 慧龍鼻大，浩曰：「真貴種矣。

translations.literal: Huilong's nose was large; Hao said: "Truly noble stock.
translations.idiomatic: Huilong's nose was large. Hao said, "Truly noble blood.

sentences.zh: 」數向諸公稱其美。

translations.literal: " He repeatedly praised his excellence before the high officials.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly praised Huilong's virtues before the high officials.

sentences.zh: 司徒長孫嵩聞之，不悅，言於世祖，以其嘆服南人，則有訕鄙國化之意。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Changsun Song heard this and was displeased; he spoke to Emperor Taiwu that, in sighing admiration for a southerner, Hao had the intention of mocking and despising the state's transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Changsun Song heard this and was displeased. He told Emperor Taiwu that by sighing in admiration over a southerner, Hao showed contempt for the state's civilizing mission.

sentences.zh: 世祖怒，召浩責之。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu was angry and summoned Hao to rebuke him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu was enraged and summoned Hao to rebuke him.

sentences.zh: 浩免冠陳謝 876 得釋。

translations.literal: Hao removed his cap and submitted an apology; text lacuna; he was released.
translations.idiomatic: Hao removed his cap and made a formal apology, and was released.

sentences.zh: 及魯宗之子軌奔姚興，後歸國，云慧龍是王愉家豎，僧彬所通生也。

translations.literal: When Lu Zong's son Gui fled to Yao Xing and later returned to the state, he said Huilong was a household servant boy of Wang Yu's family, born from relations with Seng Bin.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Zong's son Gui fled to Yao Xing and later returned to Wei, he claimed that Huilong was a household boy in Wang Yu's service, born from an illicit affair with the monk Seng Bin.

sentences.zh: 浩雖聞之，以女之故，成贊其族。

translations.literal: Although Hao heard this, for his daughter's sake he successfully vouched for his clan.
translations.idiomatic: Although Hao heard this, for his daughter's sake he successfully defended Huilong's claim to the Wang lineage.

sentences.zh: 慧龍由是不調。

translations.literal: Because of this Huilong was not promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this Huilong received no advancement.

sentences.zh: 久之，除樂安王範傅，領并荊揚三州大中正。

translations.literal: After a long time he was appointed Tutor to Prince of Le'an Fan and concurrently Chief Rectifier of Bing, Jing, and Yang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed tutor to Prince of Le'an Fan and concurrently Chief Rectifier of Bing, Jing, and Yang provinces.

sentences.zh: 慧龍抗表，願得南垂自効。

translations.literal: Huilong submitted a memorial in protest, wishing to serve on the southern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Huilong submitted a memorial in protest, asking to be sent to the southern frontier to prove his worth.

sentences.zh: 崔浩固言之，乃授南蠻校尉、安南大將軍左長史。

translations.literal: Cui Hao strongly advocated for him, and he was appointed Commandant of Southern Barbarians and Left Chief Clerk to the General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hao pressed his case, and Huilong was appointed Commandant of Southern Barbarians and Left Chief Clerk to the General Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 及劉義隆荊州刺史謝晦起兵江陵，引慧龍為援。

translations.literal: When Liu Yilong's Jing province Inspector Xie Hui raised troops at Jiangling, he called on Huilong for support.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yilong's inspector of Jing province, Xie Hui, raised troops at Jiangling, he summoned Huilong as an ally.

sentences.zh: 慧龍督司馬靈壽等一萬人拔其思陵戍，[11]進圍項城。

translations.literal: Huilong commanded Ling Shou and others with ten thousand men, captured their Silin garrison,[11] and advanced to besiege Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Huilong led Ling Shou and others with ten thousand men, captured the Silin garrison,[11] and advanced to besiege Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 晦敗，乃班師。

translations.literal: When Xie Hui was defeated, he withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie Hui was defeated, Huilong withdrew his troops.

sentences.zh: 後劉義隆將王玄謨寇滑臺，詔假慧龍楚兵將軍，與安頡等同討之。

translations.literal: Later Liu Yilong's general Wang Xuanymo attacked Huatai; an edict provisionally appointed Huilong General of Chu Troops, and he joined An Ba and others in suppressing him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liu Yilong's general Wang Xuanymo attacked Huatai. An edict provisionally appointed Huilong General of Chu Troops, and he joined An Ba and others in suppressing the invasion.

sentences.zh: 相持五十餘日，諸將以賊盛莫敢先，慧龍設奇兵大破之。

translations.literal: They faced off for more than fifty days; the generals, finding the bandits strong, dared not attack first, but Huilong deployed surprise troops and routed them completely.
translations.idiomatic: The two sides faced off for more than fifty days. The other generals, finding the enemy too strong, dared not strike first, but Huilong deployed surprise troops and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 世祖賜以劍馬錢帛，授龍驤將軍，賜爵長社侯，拜滎陽太守，仍領長史。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu bestowed sword, horse, money, and silks, appointed him General of Dragon Cavalry, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Changshe, made him Administrator of Xingyang, and he still held the chief clerkship.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu bestowed a sword, horse, money, and silks, appointed him General of Dragon Cavalry, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Changshe, made him Administrator of Xingyang, and kept him on as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 在任十年，農戰並修，大著聲績。

translations.literal: In ten years in office he developed both farming and warfare, and his reputation and achievements were great.
translations.idiomatic: In ten years in office he developed both agriculture and military readiness, and his reputation and achievements were outstanding.

sentences.zh: 招攜邊遠，歸附者萬餘家，號為善政。

translations.literal: He welcomed and settled the distant frontier; more than ten thousand households submitted, and it was called good governance.
translations.idiomatic: He drew in the distant frontier population; more than ten thousand households submitted to him, and his rule was praised as enlightened.

sentences.zh: 其後，劉義隆將到彥之、檀道濟等頻頓淮潁，大相侵掠，慧龍力戰，屢摧其鋒。

translations.literal: Thereafter Liu Yilong's generals Dao Yanzhi, Tan Daoji, and others repeatedly encamped along the Huai and Ying, launching major raids; Huilong fought hard and repeatedly broke their momentum.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Liu Yilong's generals Dao Yanzhi, Tan Daoji, and others repeatedly encamped along the Huai and Ying rivers and launched major raids. Huilong fought hard and repeatedly broke their momentum.

sentences.zh: 彥之與友人蕭斌書曰：「魯軌頑鈍，馬楚粗狂，亡人之中唯王慧龍及韓延之可為深憚。

translations.literal: Yanzhi wrote to his friend Xiao Bin: "Lu Gui is stubborn and dull, Ma Chu is crude and wild; among the exiles only Wang Huilong and Han Yanzhi are truly to be deeply feared.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi wrote to his friend Xiao Bin: "Lu Gui is stubborn and dull, Ma Chu is crude and wild. Among the exiles only Wang Huilong and Han Yanzhi are truly to be deeply feared.

sentences.zh: 不意儒生懦夫，乃令老子訝之。

translations.literal: Who would have thought that a bookish weakling would make this old man marvel at him."
translations.idiomatic: I never expected that a bookish weakling would leave this old man in awe."

sentences.zh: 」劉義隆縱反間，云慧龍自以功高而位不至，欲引寇入邊，因執安南大將軍司馬楚之以叛。

translations.literal: " Liu Yilong spread disinformation, saying Huilong, thinking his achievements great but his rank insufficient, wished to lure enemies into the borderlands, and so seized Chief Clerk to the General Who Pacifies the South Sima Chuzhi on charges of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yilong spread disinformation, claiming that Huilong, believing his achievements great but his rank too low, wished to lure enemies across the border, and on that pretext seized Chief Clerk to the General Who Pacifies the South Sima Chuzhi on charges of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 世祖聞曰：「此必不然，是齊人忌樂毅耳。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taiwu heard of it he said, "This surely cannot be true. It is like the people of Qi envying Yue Yi."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu heard of it he said, "This surely cannot be true. It is like the people of Qi envying Yue Yi."

sentences.zh: 」乃賜慧龍璽書曰：「義隆畏將軍如虎，欲相中害，朕自知之。

translations.literal: " He then bestowed on Huilong an imperial letter with the seal, saying, "Yilong fears you, General, as he would a tiger, and wishes to destroy you by scheming. I know this myself.
translations.idiomatic: He then bestowed on Huilong an imperial letter bearing the seal, saying, "Yilong fears you, General, as he would a tiger and wishes to destroy you by intrigue. I know this myself.

sentences.zh: 風塵之言，想不足介意也。

translations.literal: Rumors borne on the wind—surely they are not worth troubling over."
translations.idiomatic: Rumors borne on the wind—surely they are not worth troubling over."

sentences.zh: 」劉義隆計既不行，復遣刺客呂玄伯購慧龍首，二百戶男、絹一千匹。

translations.literal: " When Liu Yilong's plot failed, he again sent the assassin Lü Xuanbo to purchase Huilong's head for two hundred taxable male households and one thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yilong's plot failed, he again sent the assassin Lü Xuanbo to purchase Huilong's head for two hundred taxable male households and one thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 玄伯偽為反間來，求屏人有所論。

translations.literal: Xuanbo pretended to come as a disaffected agent and asked for a private audience to discuss something.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanbo pretended to come as a turncoat agent and asked for a private audience to discuss something.

sentences.zh: 慧龍疑之，使人探其懷，有尺刀。

translations.literal: Huilong grew suspicious and had someone search his robes; a foot-long knife was found.
translations.idiomatic: Huilong grew suspicious and had someone search his robes; a foot-long knife was found.

sentences.zh: 玄伯叩頭請死。

translations.literal: Xuanbo kowtowed and begged for death.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanbo kowtowed and begged to be executed.

sentences.zh: 慧龍曰：「各為其主也。

translations.literal: Huilong said, "Each man serves his own lord.
translations.idiomatic: Huilong said, "Each man serves his own lord.

sentences.zh: 吾不忍害此人。

translations.literal: I cannot bear to harm this man."
translations.idiomatic: I cannot bear to harm this man."

sentences.zh: 」左右皆言義隆賊心未已，不殺玄伯，無以制將來。

translations.literal: " Those around him all said that Yilong's treacherous intent was not yet exhausted, and that unless Xuanbo were killed there would be no restraining what might come afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Those around him all said that Yilong's treacherous intent was not yet exhausted, and that unless Xuanbo were killed there would be no deterring future assassins.

sentences.zh: 慧龍曰：「死生有命，彼亦安能害我。

translations.literal: Huilong said, "Life and death are allotted by fate. How could he harm me?
translations.idiomatic: Huilong said, "Life and death are allotted by fate. How could he harm me?

sentences.zh: 且吾方以仁義為干鹵，又何憂乎刺客。

translations.literal: Moreover, I am just now taking benevolence and righteousness as my shield and spear—why should I worry about assassins?"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, I am just now taking benevolence and righteousness as my shield and spear—why should I worry about assassins?"

sentences.zh: 」遂捨之。

translations.literal: " He then released him.
translations.idiomatic: He then released him.

sentences.zh: 時人服其寬恕。

translations.literal: People of the time admired his magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time admired his magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 慧龍自以遭難流離，常懷憂悴，乃作祭伍子胥文以寄意焉。

translations.literal: Huilong, reflecting on the hardships of exile and flight, was often weighed down with grief, and composed a Rite to Wu Zixu to voice his feelings.
translations.idiomatic: Huilong, brooding on the hardships of exile and flight, was often weighed down with grief, and composed a Rite to Wu Zixu to give his feelings expression.

sentences.zh: 生一男一女，遂絕房室。

translations.literal: He had one son and one daughter, and then ceased marital relations.
translations.idiomatic: He had one son and one daughter, and then ceased marital relations.

sentences.zh: 布衣蔬食，不參吉事。

translations.literal: Plain cloth and simple food; he took no part in festive occasions.
translations.idiomatic: He wore plain cloth and ate simple food, and took no part in festive occasions.

sentences.zh: 舉動必以禮。

translations.literal: In every movement he observed ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: In every movement he observed ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 太子少傅游雅言於朝曰：「慧龍，古之遺孝也。

translations.literal: Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent You Ya said at court, "Huilong is a surviving exemplar of the filial devotion of antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent You Ya said at court, "Huilong is a surviving exemplar of the filial devotion of antiquity."

sentences.zh: 」撰帝王制度十八篇，號曰國典。

translations.literal: He compiled eighteen chapters on the institutions of emperors and kings, entitled the National Canon.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled eighteen chapters on imperial institutions, entitled the National Canon.

sentences.zh: 真君元年，拜使持節、寧南將軍、虎牢鎮都副將。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenjun he was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General Who Pacifies the South, and Deputy Commander of Tiger Cage Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenjun he was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General Who Pacifies the South, and Deputy Commander of Tiger Cage Garrison.

sentences.zh: 未至鎮而卒。

translations.literal: Before he reached his post he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before he reached his post he died.

sentences.zh: 臨沒，謂功曹鄭曄曰：「吾覊旅南人，恩非舊結，蒙聖朝殊特之慈，得在疆埸効命。

translations.literal: At the point of death he said to Chief Clerk Zheng Ye, "I am a sojourner from the south. My ties were not old bonds, yet I received the court's extraordinary kindness and was able to give my life on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: At the point of death he said to Chief Clerk Zheng Ye, "I am a sojourner from the south. My ties were not old bonds, yet I received the court's extraordinary kindness and was able to give my life on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 誓願鞭屍吳市，戮墳江陰。

translations.literal: I had sworn to lash the corpse through the markets of Wu and desecrate the tomb beside the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: I had sworn to lash Liu Yu's corpse through the markets of Wu and desecrate his tomb beside the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 不謂嬰此重疾，有心莫遂。

translations.literal: I never expected to meet with this grave illness; my heart's wish cannot be fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: I never expected to be stricken with this grave illness; the wish of my heart cannot be fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 非唯仰愧國靈，實亦俯慚后土。

translations.literal: I am shamed not only before the state's tutelary spirits, but also before the earth below.
translations.idiomatic: I am shamed not only before the state's tutelary spirits, but also before the earth below.

sentences.zh: 修短命也，夫復何言。

translations.literal: A man's span is short—what more is there to say?
translations.idiomatic: Life is short—what more is there to say?

sentences.zh: 身歿後，乞葬河內州縣之東鄉，依古墓而不墳，足藏髮齒而已。

translations.literal: After my death I beg to be buried in the eastern township of a county in Henei commandery, following the old tombs without raising a mound—enough only to hold hair and teeth.
translations.idiomatic: After my death I beg to be buried in the eastern township of a county in Henei commandery, in the manner of the old tombs without raising a mound—enough only to hold hair and teeth.

sentences.zh: 庶魂而有知，猶希結草之報。

translations.literal: If my soul retains awareness, I still hope for the repayment of the knotting grass."
translations.idiomatic: If my soul retains awareness, I still hope for the repayment of the knotting grass."

sentences.zh: 」時制，南人入國者皆葬桑乾。

translations.literal: " At that time the regulation was that southerners who entered the state were all buried at Sanggan.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the regulation was that southerners who entered the state were all buried at Sanggan.

sentences.zh: 曄等申遺意，詔許之。

translations.literal: Ye and the others reported his final wishes, and an edict granted the request.
translations.idiomatic: Ye and the others reported his final wishes, and an edict granted the request.

sentences.zh: 贈安南將軍、荊州刺史，諡穆侯。

translations.literal: He was posthumously honored as General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Jing province, with the posthumous title Marquis Mu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Jing province, with the posthumous title Marquis Mu.

sentences.zh: 吏人及將士共於墓所起佛寺，圖慧龍及僧彬象讚之。

translations.literal: Officials, commoners, and soldiers together raised a Buddhist temple at the grave site and painted images of Huilong and Seng Bin to honor them.
translations.idiomatic: Officials, commoners, and soldiers together raised a Buddhist temple at the grave site and painted images of Huilong and Seng Bin to honor them.

sentences.zh: 呂玄伯感全宥之恩，留守墓側，終身不去。

translations.literal: Lü Xuanbo, moved by the grace of being spared, remained to guard the tomb and never left for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Xuanbo, moved by the grace of being spared, remained to guard the tomb and never left for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 子寶興襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Bao Xing inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bao Xing inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 寶興少孤，事母至孝。

translations.literal: Bao Xing lost his father young and served his mother with utmost filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Xing lost his father young and served his mother with utmost filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 尚書盧遐妻，崔浩女也。

translations.literal: He married the daughter of Minister of the Interior Lu Xia, who was Cui Hao's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: He married the daughter of Minister of the Interior Lu Xia, who was Cui Hao's daughter.

sentences.zh: 初，寶興母及遐妻俱孕，浩謂曰：「汝等將來所生，皆我之自出，可指腹為親。

translations.literal: At first, when Bao Xing's mother and Xia's wife were both pregnant, Hao said to them, "The children you will bear are all of my own flesh. You may betroth them by pointing at your bellies."
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Bao Xing's mother and Xia's wife were both pregnant, Hao said to them, "The children you will bear are all of my own flesh. You may betroth them by pointing at your bellies."

sentences.zh: 」及婚，浩為撰儀，躬自監視。

translations.literal: When the marriage took place, Hao drafted the ceremonial protocol and personally supervised it.
translations.idiomatic: When the marriage took place, Hao drafted the ceremonial protocol and personally supervised it.

sentences.zh: 謂諸客曰：「此家禮事，宜盡其美。

translations.literal: He said to the guests, "This family's rites should be carried to the fullest perfection."
translations.idiomatic: He said to the guests, "This family's rites should be carried to the fullest perfection."

sentences.zh: 」及浩被誅，盧遐後妻，寶興從母也，緣坐沒官。

translations.literal: " When Hao was executed, Lu Xia's wife—a younger wife of Xia and Bao Xing's maternal aunt—was implicated by association and enslaved as punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao was executed, Lu Xia's wife—Bao Xing's maternal aunt—was implicated by association and enslaved as punishment.

sentences.zh: 寶興亦逃避，未幾得出。

translations.literal: Bao Xing also fled into hiding, but before long was able to come out.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Xing also fled into hiding, but before long was able to emerge.

sentences.zh: 盧遐妻，時官賜度河鎮高車滑骨。

translations.literal: Lu Xia's wife had been assigned by the authorities as slave Gao Che Huagu at Duhe garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xia's wife had been assigned by the authorities as the slave Gao Che Huagu at Duhe garrison.

sentences.zh: 寶興盡賣貨產，自出塞贖之以歸。

translations.literal: Bao Xing sold all his property, went beyond the border himself to ransom her, and brought her home.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Xing sold all his property, went beyond the border himself to ransom her, and brought her home.

sentences.zh: 州辟治中從事、別駕，舉秀才，皆不就。

translations.literal: The province appointed him aide and vice director; he was nominated as Filial and Incorrupt but accepted none of these posts.
translations.idiomatic: The province appointed him aide and vice director and nominated him as Filial and Incorrupt, but he accepted none of these posts.

sentences.zh: 閉門不交人事。

translations.literal: He shut his doors and had no dealings with worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He shut his doors and had no dealings with worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 襲爵長社侯、龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: He inherited the title Marquis of Changshe and the post of General of Dragon Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title Marquis of Changshe and the post of General of Dragon Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 卒，子瓊襲爵。

translations.literal: When he died, his son Qiong inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his son Qiong inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 瓊，字世珍。

translations.literal: Qiong, courtesy name Shizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong, courtesy name Shizhen.

sentences.zh: 高祖賜名焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen bestowed the name on him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen bestowed the name on him.

sentences.zh: 太和九年，為典寺令。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Taihe he served as Director of the Palace Temple Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Taihe he served as Director of the Palace Temple Office.

sentences.zh: 十六年，降侯為伯。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year his marquisate was reduced to a count's.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year his marquisate was reduced to a count's.

sentences.zh: 高祖納其長女為嬪，拜前軍將軍、并州大中正。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen took his eldest daughter as a concubine and appointed Qiong General of the Vanguard and Chief Rectifier of Bing province.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen took his eldest daughter as a concubine and appointed Qiong General of the Vanguard and Chief Rectifier of Bing province.

sentences.zh: 正始中，為光州刺史。

translations.literal: During the Zhengshi era he served as Inspector of Guang province.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengshi era he served as Inspector of Guang province.

sentences.zh: 有受納之響，為中尉王顯所劾，終得雪免。

translations.literal: He had a reputation for accepting bribes and was impeached by Chief Commandant Wang Xian, but in the end was cleared and exonerated.
translations.idiomatic: He had a reputation for accepting bribes and was impeached by Chief Commandant Wang Xian, but in the end was cleared and exonerated.

sentences.zh: 神龜中，除左將軍、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: During the Shengui era he was appointed General of the Left and Inspector of Yan province.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shengui era he was appointed General of the Left and Inspector of Yan province.

sentences.zh: 去州歸京，多年沉滯。

translations.literal: After leaving his province he returned to the capital and for many years languished without advancement.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving his province he returned to the capital and for many years languished without advancement.

sentences.zh: 所居在司空劉騰宅西，騰雖勢傾朝野，初不候之。

translations.literal: His residence was west of Director of Works Liu Teng's mansion. Though Teng's power tilted the court and countryside, Qiong at first did not call on him.
translations.idiomatic: His residence was west of Director of Works Liu Teng's mansion. Though Teng's power tilted the court and countryside, Qiong at first did not call on him.

sentences.zh: 騰既權重，吞并隣宅，增廣舊居，唯瓊終不肯與。

translations.literal: Once Teng's authority grew heavy, he swallowed neighboring houses and expanded his old residence—but Qiong alone refused to yield.
translations.idiomatic: Once Teng's authority grew heavy, he swallowed neighboring houses and expanded his old residence—but Qiong alone refused to yield.

sentences.zh: 以此久見抑屈。

translations.literal: For this reason he long remained suppressed and passed over.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason he long remained suppressed and passed over.

sentences.zh: 瓊女適范陽盧道亮，不聽歸其夫家。

translations.literal: Qiong's daughter was married to Lu Daoliang of Fanyang, but Qiong would not let her return to her husband's home.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong's daughter was married to Lu Daoliang of Fanyang, but Qiong would not let her return to her husband's home.

sentences.zh: 及女卒，哀慟無已。

translations.literal: When the daughter died he grieved without end.
translations.idiomatic: When the daughter died he grieved without end.

sentences.zh: 瓊仍葬之別所，冢不即塞，常於壙內哭泣。

translations.literal: Qiong buried her in a separate place, did not immediately seal the tomb, and often wept inside the burial chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong buried her in a separate place, did not immediately seal the tomb, and often wept inside the burial chamber.

sentences.zh: 久之乃掩。

translations.literal: Only after a long time did he cover it over.
translations.idiomatic: Only after a long time did he cover it over.

sentences.zh: 當時深怪，疑其穢行。

translations.literal: People at the time were deeply astonished and suspected improper conduct.
translations.idiomatic: People at the time were deeply astonished and suspected improper conduct.

sentences.zh: 加以聾疾，每見道俗，乞丐無已。

translations.literal: Added to this was deafness; whenever he saw monks or laymen he begged from them without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Added to this was deafness; whenever he saw monks or laymen he begged from them without cease.

sentences.zh: 造次見之，令人笑愕。

translations.literal: Encountering him casually, one could not help laughing in amazement.
translations.idiomatic: Encountering him casually, one could not help laughing in amazement.

sentences.zh: 道逢太保、廣平王懷，據鞍抗禮，自言馬瘦。

translations.literal: On the road he met Grand Tutor Prince of Guangping Huai, saluted from the saddle in equal posture, and said his horse was lean.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he met Grand Tutor Prince of Guangping Huai, saluted from the saddle as an equal, and said his horse was lean.

sentences.zh: 懷即以誕馬并乘具與之。

translations.literal: Huai at once gave him Dan's horse together with its riding gear.
translations.idiomatic: Huai at once gave him Dan's horse together with its riding gear.

sentences.zh: 嘗詣尚書令李崇，騎馬至其黃閤，見崇子世哲，直問繼伯在否。

translations.literal: Once he called on Minister of the Interior Li Chong, riding his horse right up to the Yellow Gate, and seeing Chong's son Shizhe bluntly asked whether Jibo was present.
translations.idiomatic: Once he called on Minister of the Interior Li Chong, riding his horse right up to the Yellow Gate, and seeing Chong's son Shizhe bluntly asked whether Jibo was present.

sentences.zh: 崇趨出，瓊乃下。

translations.literal: Chong hurried out, and only then did Qiong dismount.
translations.idiomatic: Chong hurried out, and only then did Qiong dismount.

sentences.zh: 崇儉而好以紙帖衣領，瓊哂而掣去之。

translations.literal: Chong was frugal and liked to paste paper on his collar; Qiong laughed and tore it off.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was frugal and liked to paste paper on his collar; Qiong laughed and tore it off.

sentences.zh: 崇小子青肫，嘗盛服。

translations.literal: Chong's youngest son Qingzhun once dressed in splendid attire.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's youngest son Qingzhun once dressed in splendid attire.

translations.literal: Text lacuna in the manuscript.
translations.idiomatic: Text missing in the manuscript.

sentences.zh: 寵勢亦不足恨。

translations.literal: Even pampering and power were nothing to envy.
translations.idiomatic: Even pampering and power were nothing to envy.

sentences.zh: 領軍元叉使奴遺瓊馬，并留奴。

translations.literal: General-in-Chief Yuan Cha sent a servant to present Qiong with a horse and left the servant behind.
translations.idiomatic: General-in-Chief Yuan Cha sent a servant to present Qiong with a horse and left the servant behind.

sentences.zh: 王誦聞之，笑曰：「東海之風，於茲墜矣。

translations.literal: Wang Song heard of it and laughed, saying, "The wind of the Eastern Sea has fallen here at last."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Song heard of it and laughed, saying, "The wind of the Eastern Sea has fallen here at last."

sentences.zh: 」孝昌三年，除鎮東將軍、金紫光祿大夫、中書令。

translations.literal: " In the third year of Xiaochang he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and Director of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xiaochang he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and Director of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時瓊子遵業為黃門郎，故有此授。

translations.literal: At that time Qiong's son Zunye was a Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, which is why he received this appointment.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Qiong's son Zunye was a Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, which is why he received this appointment.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十四。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 贈征北將軍、中書監、并州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously honored as General Who Campaigns North, Supervisor of the Central Secretariat, and Inspector of Bing province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as General Who Campaigns North, Supervisor of the Central Secretariat, and Inspector of Bing province.

sentences.zh: 自慧龍入國，三世一身，至瓊始有四子。

translations.literal: From the time Huilong entered the state, three generations had each produced only one son; only with Qiong did the line first have four sons.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Huilong entered Wei, three generations had each produced only one son; only with Qiong did the line first have four sons.

sentences.zh: 長子遵業，風儀清秀，涉歷經史。

translations.literal: The eldest son Zunye had elegant bearing and a refined appearance, and had traversed the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son, Zunye, was refined in bearing and well read in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 位著作佐郎，與司徒左長史崔鴻同撰起居注。

translations.literal: He held the post of Associate Gentleman of the Palace Library, and together with Cui Hong, Left Chief Clerk to the Minister over the Masses, compiled the Daily Record.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Associate Gentleman of the Palace Library and, together with Cui Hong, Left Chief Clerk to the Minister over the Masses, helped compile the Daily Record.

sentences.zh: 遷右軍將軍，兼散騎常侍，慰勞蠕蠕。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Right Army, concurrently Regular Attendant at the Dispersed Cavalry, and went to console the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General of the Right Army and concurrently Regular Attendant at the Dispersed Cavalry, and was sent to offer condolences to the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 乃詣代京，採拾遺文，以補起居所闕。

translations.literal: He then went to the capital at Dai, gathered lost texts, and used them to fill lacunae in the Daily Record.
translations.idiomatic: He then traveled to the capital at Dai, collected surviving documents, and used them to fill gaps in the Daily Record.

sentences.zh: 與崔光、安豐王延明等參定服章。

translations.literal: Together with Cui Guang, Prince of Anfeng Yanming, and others, he helped establish official dress regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Cui Guang, Prince of Anfeng Yanming, and others, he helped draft regulations for official dress.

sentences.zh: 及光為肅宗講孝經，遵業預講，延業錄義，[12]並應詔作釋奠侍宴詩。

translations.literal: When Guang lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety for Emperor Suzong, Zunye took part in the lecture and Yanye recorded the meaning,[12] and both responded to the imperial edict with poems for the sacrificial feast banquet.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Guang lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety for Emperor Suzong, Zunye joined the lecture and Yanye recorded its substance,[12] and both wrote poems at the emperor's command for the libation feast.

sentences.zh: 時人語曰：「英英濟濟，王家兄弟。

translations.literal: People of the time said, "Splendid and abundant, the Wang brothers."
translations.idiomatic: People at the time said, "Splendid and accomplished—the Wang brothers.

sentences.zh: 」轉司徒左長史、黃門郎、監典儀注。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to Left Chief Clerk of the Minister over the Masses, Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, and Supervisor of Canonical Rites and Protocol.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Left Chief Clerk of the Minister over the Masses, Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, and Supervisor of Canonical Rites and Protocol.

sentences.zh: 遵業有譽當時，與中書令陳郡袁翻、尚書瑯琊王誦並領黃門郎，號曰三哲。

translations.literal: Zunye had a reputation in his time; together with Director of the Central Secretariat Yuan Fan of Chen commandery and Secretary Wang Song of Langya, all holding the post of Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, they were called the Three Sages.
translations.idiomatic: Zunye was widely admired in his day. Together with Director of the Central Secretariat Yuan Fan of Chen commandery and Secretary Wang Song of Langya, all serving as Gentlemen at the Yellow Gate, they were known as the Three Sages.

sentences.zh: 時政歸門下，世謂侍中、黃門為小宰相。

translations.literal: At that time governmental affairs belonged to the Gate Office, and the age called the Attendant-in-Chief and the Yellow Gate "lesser chancellors."
translations.idiomatic: At that time real power lay with the Gate Office, and people spoke of the Attendant-in-Chief and the Yellow Gate as "lesser chancellors."

sentences.zh: 而遵業從容恬素，若處丘園。

translations.literal: Yet Zunye was easy and plain, as if dwelling in hills and gardens.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zunye remained easy and unassuming, as though he lived in seclusion on some country hillside.

sentences.zh: 嘗著穿角履，好事者多毀新履以學之。

translations.literal: Once he wore pointed-toe shoes with cut corners; many enthusiasts ruined new shoes trying to imitate him.
translations.idiomatic: He once wore shoes with splayed, cut-away toes, and many fashion-minders ruined new pairs trying to copy him.

sentences.zh: 以胡太后臨朝，天下方亂，謀避地，自求徐州。

translations.literal: Because Empress Dowager Hu held court and the realm was on the verge of disorder, he planned to flee to safety and requested Xuzhou for himself.
translations.idiomatic: With Empress Dowager Hu governing from behind the curtain and the realm descending into chaos, he sought a refuge and asked to be sent to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「王誦罷幽州始作黃門，卿何乃欲徐州？

translations.literal: The empress dowager said, "Wang Song only left You province before taking up the Yellow Gate post—why do you want Xuzhou?
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager said, "Wang Song had to leave You province before he could take up the Yellow Gate post—why are you asking for Xuzhou?

sentences.zh: 更待一二年，當有好處分。

translations.literal: Wait another year or two, and you will surely receive a fine appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Wait another year or two, and you will surely receive a fine appointment."

sentences.zh: 」遵業兄弟，並交遊時俊，乃為當時所美。

translations.literal: " The Zunye brothers all kept company with the worthies of the age and were admired by their contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: The Zunye brothers kept company with the leading men of the age and were widely admired.

sentences.zh: 及尒朱榮入洛，兄弟在父喪中，以於莊帝有從姨兄弟之親，相率奉迎，俱見害河陰。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang, the brothers were in mourning for their father; because they were maternal cousins of Emperor Zhuang, they went out together to welcome him, and all were killed at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang, the brothers were still in mourning for their father. Because they were maternal cousins of Emperor Zhuang, they went out together to welcome him—and all were killed at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 議者惜其人才，而譏其躁競。

translations.literal: Commentators regretted their talent but mocked their rash ambition.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators regretted their gifts but faulted their hasty ambition.

sentences.zh: 贈并州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously honored as Inspector of Bing province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Inspector of Bing province.

sentences.zh: 著三晉記十卷。

translations.literal: He authored Records of the Three Jin in ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Records of the Three Jin in ten juan.

sentences.zh: 遵業子松年，尚書庫部郎。

translations.literal: Zunye's son Songnian was a Gentleman of the Treasury Section in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Zunye's son Songnian served as Gentleman of the Treasury Section in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 韓延之，字顯宗，南陽赭陽人，魏司徒暨之後也。

translations.literal: Han Yanzhi, courtesy name Xianzong, was a native of Zheyang in Nanyang, a descendant of Ji, Minister over the Masses of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yanzhi, courtesy name Xianzong, was a native of Zheyang in Nanyang and a descendant of Ji, Minister over the Masses of Wei.

sentences.zh: 司馬德宗平西府錄事參軍。

translations.literal: He was Recording Officer in the staff of Sima Dezong, Prince who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Recording Officer on the staff of Sima Dezong, Prince Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 劉裕率伐司馬休之，[13]未至江陵，密使與延之書招之。

translations.literal: Liu Yu led troops to attack Sima Xiuzhi,[13] and before reaching Jiangling sent a secret messenger with a letter to win Yanzhi over.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu marched against Sima Xiuzhi,[13] and before he reached Jiangling he sent a secret messenger with a letter trying to win Yanzhi over.

sentences.zh: 延之報曰：「聞親率戎馬，遠履西畿，闔境士庶，莫不怪駭。

translations.literal: Yanzhi replied, "I hear that you personally lead troops, traveling far into the western capital region; within the borders none of the gentry or common people is not astonished and alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi replied, "I hear that you have personally led your troops deep into the western capital region, and every official and commoner within the borders is astonished and alarmed.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 莫知師出之名故也。

translations.literal: Because no one knows the name or reason for the army's campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Because no one knows the proper name for this campaign.

sentences.zh: 司馬平西體國忠貞，款愛待物，當於古人中求耳。

translations.literal: Sima, Prince who Pacifies the West, embodies loyalty to the state and treats others with sincerity and kindness—one must seek his equal among the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: Sima, Prince Who Pacifies the West, embodies loyalty to the state and treats others with sincerity and warmth—a man to be sought among the ancients alone.

sentences.zh: 劉裕足下，海內之人誰不見足下此心，而復欲欺誑國士，天地所不容，在彼不在此矣。

translations.literal: Liu Yu, sir—who under heaven does not see your heart? Yet you again wish to deceive a man of the state. Heaven and earth will not tolerate it; the fault lies with you, not with me.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu—who under heaven does not see through your intent? Yet you would again try to deceive a man of honor. Heaven and earth will not abide it; the blame lies with you, not with me.

sentences.zh: 今伐人之君，啗人以利，真可謂處懷期物，自有由來者矣。

translations.literal: Now attacking another man's lord and baiting men with profit—this truly may be called harboring designs and waiting upon opportunity; it has its origins after all.
translations.idiomatic: To attack another man's sovereign and lure men with profit—this truly shows a heart that has long schemed for power; it is nothing new.

sentences.zh: 以平西之至德，寧無授命之臣乎？

translations.literal: With the Prince who Pacifies the West's supreme virtue, could there fail to be ministers who would give their lives for him?
translations.idiomatic: With the Prince Who Pacifies the West's supreme virtue, could he fail to command ministers who would give their lives for him?

sentences.zh: 假令天長喪亂，九流渾濁，當與臧洪遊於地下，不復多言。

translations.literal: Even if heaven long endures chaos and the nine ranks are muddied, I would yet keep company with Zang Hong in the underworld—no more need be said.
translations.idiomatic: Even if heaven prolongs the age of chaos and every walk of life grows corrupt, I would yet keep company with Zang Hong in the grave—I will say no more.

sentences.zh: 」裕得書歎息，以示諸佐曰：「事人當應如此。

translations.literal: " When Yu received the letter he sighed and showed it to his aides, saying, "Serving another man ought to be like this.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu received the letter he sighed and showed it to his staff, saying, "This is how one ought to serve one's lord.

sentences.zh: 」劉裕父名翹，字顯宗，於是延之字顯宗，名子為翹，蓋示不臣劉氏也。

translations.literal: " Liu Yu's father's name was Qiao and his courtesy name Xianzong; thereupon Yanzhi took the courtesy name Xianzong and named his son Qiao, plainly showing that he would not serve the Liu house.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu's father's name was Qiao and his courtesy name Xianzong; Yanzhi therefore took the courtesy name Xianzong and named his son Qiao, plainly declaring that he would not submit to the Liu house.

sentences.zh: 後奔姚興。

translations.literal: Later he fled to Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Later he fled to Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 泰常二年，與司馬文思來入國，以延之為虎牢鎮將，爵魯陽侯。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taichang, he came into the state together with Sima Wensi and was made Garrison Commander of Hulao, enfeoffed as Marquis of Luyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taichang he entered Wei together with Sima Wensi; Yanzhi was made Garrison Commander of Hulao and enfeoffed as Marquis of Luyang.

sentences.zh: 初延之曾來往栢谷塢，省魯宗之墓，有終焉之志。

translations.literal: Earlier Yanzhi had traveled back and forth to Cypress Valley Fort, visited the tomb of Lu Zongzhi, and had the desire to end his days there.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Yanzhi had traveled to Cypress Valley Fort, visited the tomb of Lu Zongzhi, and resolved to end his days there.

sentences.zh: 因謂子孫云：「河洛三代所都，必有治於此者。

translations.literal: He therefore told his descendants, "The Yellow River and Luoyang region was the capital of three dynasties; there must one day be good government here again.
translations.idiomatic: He told his descendants, "The lands of the Yellow River and Luoyang were the seat of three dynasties; there must someday be good government here again.

sentences.zh: 我死不勞向北代葬也，即可就此。

translations.literal: When I die, do not trouble yourselves to bury me north in Dai; you may simply do it here.
translations.idiomatic: When I die, do not trouble yourselves to bury me north in Dai—bury me here."

sentences.zh: 」及卒，子從其言，遂葬於宗之墓次。

translations.literal: " When he died, his son followed his words and buried him beside Zongzhi's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his son followed his wishes and buried him beside Zongzhi's tomb.

sentences.zh: 延之死後五十餘年而高祖徙都，其孫即居於墓北栢谷塢。

translations.literal: More than fifty years after Yanzhi's death, Emperor Gaozu moved the capital, and his grandson then took up residence north of the tomb at Cypress Valley Fort.
translations.idiomatic: More than fifty years after Yanzhi's death, Emperor Gaozu moved the capital, and his grandson settled north of the tomb at Cypress Valley Fort.

sentences.zh: 延之前妻羅氏生子措，措隨父入國。

translations.literal: Yanzhi's former wife, Lady Luo, bore a son Cuo; Cuo followed his father into the state.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi's first wife, Lady Luo, bore a son named Cuo, who followed his father into Wei.

sentences.zh: 又以淮南王女妻延之，生道仁。

translations.literal: A daughter of the Prince of Huainan was also given to Yanzhi in marriage, and she bore Daoren.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi also took a daughter of the Prince of Huainan as his wife, and she bore Daoren.

sentences.zh: 措推道仁為嫡，襲父爵，位至殿中尚書。

translations.literal: Cuo yielded the status of legitimate heir to Daoren, who inherited his father's title and rose to Palace Secretary within the Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Cuo yielded primogeniture to Daoren, who inherited his father's title and rose to Palace Secretary within the Hall.

sentences.zh: 進爵西平公。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Duke of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Duke of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 袁式，字季祖，陳郡陽夏人，漢司徒滂之後。

translations.literal: Yuan Shi, courtesy name Jizu, was a native of Yangxia in Chen commandery, a descendant of Pang, Minister over the Masses of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shi, courtesy name Jizu, was a native of Yangxia in Chen commandery and a descendant of Pang, Minister over the Masses of Han.

sentences.zh: 父淵，司馬昌明侍中。

translations.literal: His father Yuan served as Attendant-in-Chief under Sima Changming.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuan served as Attendant-in-Chief under Sima Changming.

sentences.zh: 式在南，歷武陵王遵諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Shi was in the south and successively served as Consultation Officer on the staff of Prince Zun of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: In the south Shi served as Consultation Officer on the staff of Prince Zun of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 與司馬文思等歸姚興。

translations.literal: Together with Sima Wensi and others he submitted to Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Sima Wensi and others he went over to Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 泰常二年歸國，為上客，賜爵陽夏子。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taichang he returned to the state, was treated as a senior guest, and was granted the title Viscount of Yangxia.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taichang he returned to Wei, was received as a senior guest, and was granted the title Viscount of Yangxia.

sentences.zh: 與司徒崔浩一面，便盡國士之交。

translations.literal: With one meeting with Minister of Works Cui Hao, he became intimate as a true companion of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: After a single meeting with Minister of Works Cui Hao, the two became intimate friends in the full sense of the term.

sentences.zh: 是時，朝儀典章，悉出於浩，浩以式博於古事，每所草創，恒顧訪之。

translations.literal: At that time court ritual and canonical regulations all came from Hao; because Shi was broad in ancient affairs, whenever Hao drafted something new he always consulted him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time court ritual and institutional regulations all issued from Cui Hao, and because Shi was deeply versed in antiquity, Hao invariably sought his counsel whenever he drafted anything new.

sentences.zh: 性長者，雖羈旅飄泊，而清貧守度，不失士節，時人甚敬重之，皆呼曰袁諮議。

translations.literal: By nature a man of integrity, though living as a wanderer in exile he remained poor but kept proper measure and did not lose a gentleman's principles; people of the time greatly respected him and all called him Adviser Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: A man of integrity by nature, he remained poor but dignified even in exile, never abandoning a gentleman's standards; his contemporaries held him in high esteem and called him Adviser Yuan.

sentences.zh: 延和二年，衞大將軍、樂安王範為雍州刺史，詔式與中書侍郎高允俱為從事中郎，[14]辭而獲免。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yanhe, when General-in-Chief Fan, Prince of Le'an, was Inspector of Yong province, an edict ordered Shi and Gao Yun, Vice Director of the Central Secretariat, both to serve as Attending Clerks;[14] he declined and was excused.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yanhe, when General-in-Chief Fan, Prince of Le'an, became Inspector of Yong province, an edict appointed Shi and Gao Yun, Vice Director of the Central Secretariat, as Attending Clerks;[14] Shi declined and was excused.

sentences.zh: 式沉靖樂道，周覽書傳，至於詁訓、倉、雅，偏所留懷。

translations.literal: Shi was calm and serene and loved the Way; he surveyed books and chronicles broadly, and especially cherished the glossaries, the Cangjie primer, and the Erya.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was calm and devoted to learning; he read widely in books and chronicles, with a special fondness for glossaries, the Cangjie primer, and the Erya.

sentences.zh: 作字釋，未就。

translations.literal: He wrote a Character Explanations, but it was not completed.
translations.idiomatic: He began a work called Character Explanations but did not finish it.

sentences.zh: 以天安二年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Tian'an.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Tian'an.

sentences.zh: 贈豫州刺史，諡肅侯。

translations.literal: He was posthumously honored as Inspector of Yu province and given the posthumous title Marquis Su.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Inspector of Yu province with the posthumous title Marquis Su.

sentences.zh: 子濟，襲。

translations.literal: His son Ji inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ji inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 位魏郡太守，政有清稱，加寧遠將軍。

translations.literal: He reached the post of Administrator of Wei commandery, was famed for clean governance, and was additionally made General Who Pacifies the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Administrator of Wei commandery, won a reputation for upright governance, and was additionally appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance.

sentences.zh: 子姪遂居潁川之陽夏。

translations.literal: His sons and nephews thereupon settled at Yangxia in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: His sons and nephews then settled at Yangxia in Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：刁雍才識恢遠，著聲立事，禮遇優隆，世有人爵堂構之義也。

translations.literal: The court historian says: Diao Yong's talent and insight were vast and far-reaching; he made a name and established deeds; he received outstanding favor—his line embodied the meaning of inheriting human rank and building the hall-frame.
translations.idiomatic: The court historian writes: Diao Yong's talent and vision were far-reaching; he won renown and accomplished real deeds, and received the highest favor—a family that truly embodied the promise of inheriting office and building a lasting house.

sentences.zh: 王慧龍拔難自歸，頗歷夷險，撫人督眾，見憚嚴敵。

translations.literal: Wang Huilong extricated himself from hardship and returned of his own accord, passed through many dangers, soothed the people and commanded troops, and was feared by stern enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huilong escaped hardship to return of his own accord, endured many trials, governed men and led armies, and was feared even by formidable foes.

sentences.zh: 世珍實有令子，克播家聲。

translations.literal: Shizhen truly had fine sons who were able to spread the family's renown.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhen truly had worthy sons who carried on the family's name.

sentences.zh: 韓延之報書劉裕，國體在焉。

translations.literal: Han Yanzhi's reply to Liu Yu contained the spirit of the state itself.
translations.idiomatic: In Han Yanzhi's letter to Liu Yu, the integrity of the state itself was at stake.

sentences.zh: 袁式贊禮崔浩，時稱長者，一時有稱，信為美哉。

translations.literal: Yuan Shi assisted Cui Hao in ritual matters, was called a man of integrity in his time, had repute for a time—truly admirable.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shi advised Cui Hao on ritual, was acclaimed as a man of integrity in his day, and earned enduring praise—truly admirable.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Textual collation notes.
translations.idiomatic: Collation Notes

sentences.zh: 南阻大

translations.literal: southward blocked Great
translations.idiomatic: "south of Great [Mountain]" — the passage in question.

translations.literal: Text lacuna in the manuscript.
translations.idiomatic: Text missing in the manuscript.

sentences.zh: 李慈銘云：「『大』下當是『峴』字。」

translations.literal: Li Ciming states: "Below 'Great' there ought to be the character 'Xian.'"
translations.idiomatic: Li Ciming remarked: "After 'Great' the character should be 'Xian' [forming Mount Daxiang]."

sentences.zh: 朝於行觀 北史卷二六刁雍傳「觀」作「宮」，疑是。

translations.literal: "Attending at the Traveling View" — in the Diao Yong biography in Beishi juan 26, "View" is written "Palace"; probably correct.
translations.idiomatic: "Attending at the Traveling View": in the biography of Diao Yong in Beishi, juan 26, "View" is written "Palace"; this is probably correct.

sentences.zh: 此城已平 李慈銘云：「『此』當作『北』。

translations.literal: "This city was already pacified" — Li Ciming states: "'This' should be 'North.'"
translations.idiomatic: "This city was already pacified": Li Ciming remarked, "'This' should read 'North.'"

sentences.zh: 」按上有「平其北城」語，李說是。

translations.literal: " Examining above, there is the phrase "pacified its north city"; Li's view is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Above there is the phrase "pacified its north city"; Li's view is correct.

sentences.zh: 高於水不過一丈 通典卷一水利田引雍表「水」上有「河」字。

translations.literal: "Higher than the water by no more than one zhang" — Tongdian juan 1, Water and Fields, citing Yong's memorial, has the character "river" before "water."
translations.idiomatic: "Higher than the water by no more than one zhang": Tongdian, juan 1 (Water and Fields), citing Diao Yong's memorial, has the graph "river" before "water."

sentences.zh: 按下云：「高於河水二丈三尺。

translations.literal: Examining below, it says: "Higher than the river water by two zhang and three chi.
translations.idiomatic: Below the text reads, "Higher than the river water by two zhang and three chi."

sentences.zh: 」疑此脫「河」字。

translations.literal: " It is suspected that here the character "river" is missing.
translations.idiomatic: It is suspected that "river" has been omitted here.

sentences.zh: 王政有闕所致也 諸本脫「所」字，今據冊府卷五八０

translations.literal: "Caused by lacunae in royal governance" — all editions omit the character "that which"; now according to Cefu juan 580
translations.idiomatic: "Caused by lacunae in royal governance": all editions omit "that which"; restored according to Cefu, juan 580

sentences.zh: 〈六九五三頁〉

translations.literal: (page 6953)

sentences.zh: 補。

translations.literal: supplemented.
translations.idiomatic: is supplemented here.

sentences.zh: 太和中例降為侯 按卷四下世祖紀下太平真君三年九月見「東安公刁雍」，墓誌集釋刁遵墓誌

translations.literal: "In the Taihe era, by regulation demoted to marquis" — examining juan 4B Basic Annals of Shizu, ninth month of the third year of Taiping Zhenjun, one finds "Diao Yong, Duke of Dong'an"; Collected Epitaph Interpretations, epitaph of Diao Zun
translations.idiomatic: "In the Taihe era, by regulation demoted to marquis": in juan 4B of the Basic Annals of Emperor Shizu, ninth month of the third year of Taiping Zhenjun, we find "Diao Yong, Duke of Dong'an"; in the Collected Epitaph Interpretations, the epitaph of Diao Zun

sentences.zh: 〈圖版二二二〉

translations.literal: (Plate 222)
translations.idiomatic: (Plate 222)

sentences.zh: 稱雍為「東安簡公」。

translations.literal: calls Yong "Duke Jian of Dong'an."
translations.idiomatic: styles Diao Yong "Duke Jian of Dong'an."

sentences.zh: 是刁雍先曾進封為公，雍傳失書，這裏所謂「例降為侯」，便不可解。

translations.literal: This shows that Diao Yong had earlier been advanced to duke; the Yong biography failed to record it, and therefore the phrase here "by regulation demoted to marquis" becomes unintelligible.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that Diao Yong had previously been ennobled as a duke; because the biography omits that fact, the phrase "by regulation demoted to marquis" here becomes unintelligible.

sentences.zh: 子沖字文助 北史卷二六「助」作「朗」，本書卷八四儒林刁沖傳

translations.literal: "His son Chong, courtesy name Wenzhu" — Beishi juan 26 writes "Zhu" as "Lang"; this book's juan 84, Confucian scholars, biography of Diao Chong
translations.idiomatic: "His son Chong, courtesy name Wenzhu": Beishi, juan 26, writes "Zhu" as "Lang"; the biography of Diao Chong in juan 84 of the Confucian scholars section of this book

translations.literal: (Supplement)
translations.idiomatic: (Supplement)

sentences.zh: 也作「朗」，疑「助」乃「朗」之訛。

translations.literal: also writes "Lang"; it is suspected that "Zhu" is a corruption of "Lang."
translations.idiomatic: also reads "Lang"; "Zhu" is probably a corruption of "Lang."

sentences.zh: 相州刺史中山王熙在鄴起兵 諸本「中山」作「山陽」。

translations.literal: "Inspector of Xiang province, Prince of Zhongshan Xi, raised troops at Ye" — all editions write "Zhongshan" as "Shanyang."
translations.idiomatic: "Inspector of Xiang province, Prince Xi of Zhongshan, raised troops at Ye": all editions read "Zhongshan" as "Shanyang."

sentences.zh: 按卷一九下熙傳和其他紀載熙襲中山王，從未封山陽王，今改正。

translations.literal: Examining juan 19B biography of Xi and other records, Xi inherited the title Prince of Zhongshan and was never enfeoffed Prince of Shanyang; corrected now.
translations.idiomatic: According to the biography of Xi in juan 19B and other records, Xi inherited the title Prince of Zhongshan and was never made Prince of Shanyang; the text is corrected accordingly.

sentences.zh: 送整與弟宣及子恭等幽繫之 諸本「宣」作「宜」。

translations.literal: "Sent Zheng together with his younger brother Xuan and his son Gong and others to be imprisoned in secret" — all editions write "Xuan" as "Yi."
translations.idiomatic: "Sent Zheng together with his younger brother Xuan and his son Gong and others to be imprisoned": all editions read "Xuan" as "Yi."

sentences.zh: 按下文刁雙傳作「宣」，北史卷二六刁雙傳同。

translations.literal: Examining below, the biography of Diao Shuang writes "Xuan"; Beishi juan 26, biography of Diao Shuang, agrees.
translations.idiomatic: The biography of Diao Shuang below reads "Xuan," as does Beishi, juan 26, biography of Diao Shuang.

sentences.zh: 刁遵墓誌陰錄諸子名也作「宣」。

translations.literal: The rear inscription on Diao Zun's epitaph listing the sons' names also writes "Xuan."
translations.idiomatic: The rear inscription on Diao Zun's epitaph, listing the names of his sons, also has "Xuan."

sentences.zh: 「宜」字形近而訛，今改正。

translations.literal: The character "Yi" is graphically close and is a corruption; corrected now.
translations.idiomatic: "Yi" is a graphic corruption of "Xuan"; the text is corrected accordingly.

sentences.zh: 遷驃騎大將軍左光祿大夫 北史卷二九「驃」作「驍」。

translations.literal: "Transferred to General of Fast Cavalry, Great General, and Left Grand Master of the Palace" — Beishi juan 29 writes "Biao" as "Xiao."
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to General Who Chases the Enemy and Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness: Beishi juan 29 reads the title character biao as xiao (Valiant Cavalry General).

sentences.zh: 按卷一一三官氏志載太和後品令驍騎將軍在第四品，既無加「大」之例，也不能兼第二品的左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Examining juan 113 Treatise on Official Surnames, the post-Taihe rank regulations place General of Vigorous Cavalry in the fourth rank; there is no precedent for adding "Great," nor can one concurrently hold Left Grand Master of the Palace of the second rank.
translations.idiomatic: According to juan 113 of the Treatise on Official Surnames, the post-Taihe rank regulations place General of Vigorous Cavalry in the fourth rank; there is no precedent for adding "Great," and the post could not be held concurrently with Left Grand Master of the Palace, a second-rank office.

sentences.zh: 「驍」字訛。

translations.literal: The character "Xiao" is a corruption.
translations.idiomatic: "Xiao" is a textual corruption.

sentences.zh: 但下文說雙死後「贈車騎大將軍、儀同三司」。

translations.literal: But below it says that after Shuang's death he was posthumously granted "Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, with the honors of the Three Preceptors."
translations.idiomatic: Yet below we read that after Shuang's death he was posthumously honored as Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry with the honors of the Three Preceptors.

sentences.zh: 「驃騎」班在「車騎」上，一般不可能贈官反低於身前所任官職。

translations.literal: "Fast Cavalry" ranks above "Chariots and Cavalry"; generally it is impossible for a posthumous honor to be lower than the office held in life.
translations.idiomatic: General of Fast Cavalry outranks Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry; a posthumous honor would not normally rank below the office held in life.

sentences.zh: 這裏當衍「大」字，驃騎將軍兼左光祿大夫魏末多見。

translations.literal: Here the character "Great" should be considered superfluous; General of Fast Cavalry concurrently holding Left Grand Master of the Palace was common at the end of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The character "Great" should be regarded as an interpolation here; General of Fast Cavalry concurrently serving as Left Grand Master of the Palace was common in the late Wei period.

sentences.zh: 慧龍督司馬靈壽等一萬人拔其思陵戍 諸本「靈」作「盧」，北史卷三五王慧龍傳作「靈」。

translations.literal: "Huilong supervised Sima Lingshou and ten thousand men in capturing their Silin garrison" — all editions write "Ling" as "Lu"; Beishi juan 35, biography of Wang Huilong, writes "Ling."
translations.idiomatic: "Huilong supervised Sima Lingshou and ten thousand men in capturing the Silin garrison": all editions read "Ling" as "Lu"; Beishi, juan 35, biography of Wang Huilong, has "Ling."

sentences.zh: 按卷三七司馬叔璠傳附長子靈壽，「盧」字訛，今據改。

translations.literal: Examining juan 37 biography of Sima Shufan, appended eldest son Lingshou; the character "Lu" is a corruption; corrected now according to this evidence.
translations.idiomatic: According to juan 37, biography of Sima Shufan, appended section on his eldest son Lingshou, "Lu" is corrupt; the text is emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 遵業預講延業錄義 諸本「延業」作「延明」，北史卷三五作「延業」。

translations.literal: "Zunye attended the lecture and Yanye recorded the meaning" — all editions read "Yanye" as "Yanming"; Beishi juan 35 has "Yanye."
translations.idiomatic: Zunye attended the lecture and Yanye recorded the meaning: all editions read Yanye as Yanming, but Beishi juan 35 has Yanye.

sentences.zh: 按下云：「英英濟濟，王家兄弟。

translations.literal: The text below says: "Splendid and numerous, the Wang brothers."
translations.idiomatic: The passage below says, Splendid and numerous, the Wang brothers.

sentences.zh: 」延業是遵業第二弟，見北史卷三五，若是元延明，和所謂「王家兄弟」不合。

translations.literal: " Yanye was Zunye's second younger brother, seen in Beishi juan 35; if it were Yuan Yanming, it would not fit the so-called "Wang brothers."
translations.idiomatic: Yanye was Zunye's second younger brother, as seen in Beishi juan 35. If the name referred to Yuan Yanming, it would not fit the phrase Wang brothers.

sentences.zh: 「明」字涉上「安豐王延明」而訛，今據北史改。

translations.literal: The character "ming" was corrupted through contamination from "Prince of Anfeng Yanming" above; now corrected according to Beishi.
translations.idiomatic: The character ming was corrupted by association with Prince of Anfeng Yanming above; it is now corrected according to Beishi.

sentences.zh: 又按此傳王瓊四子，只舉遵業一人，傳中却一再稱王家兄弟。

translations.literal: Moreover, examining this biography, Wang Qiong had four sons, yet only Zunye alone is cited, while within the biography the Wang brothers are repeatedly mentioned.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, this biography says Wang Qiong had four sons yet names only Zunye, while repeatedly referring to the Wang brothers.

sentences.zh: 北史傳末附見遵業弟廣業、延業、季和，皆魏書所宜有，疑此傳脫去。

translations.literal: At the end of the Beishi biography are appended Zunye's younger brothers Guangye, Yanye, and Jihe, all of which the Wei shu ought to have; it is suspected this biography has omissions.
translations.idiomatic: The Beishi biography appends at its end Zunye's younger brothers Guangye, Yanye, and Jihe, all of whom the Wei shu ought to include; this biography likely has lacunae.

sentences.zh: 劉裕率伐司馬休之 按北史卷二七韓延之傳無「率」字。

translations.literal: "Liu Yu led a campaign against Sima Xiuzhi" — according to Beishi juan 27, Biography of Han Yanzhi, there is no character "shuai."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu led a campaign against Sima Xiuzhi: Beishi juan 27, Biography of Han Yanzhi, lacks the word shuai (lead).

sentences.zh: 張森楷云：「此句殊費解，疑『率』下當有『兵』字。

translations.literal: Zhang Senkai remarked: "This sentence is especially hard to understand; it is suspected that below 'shuai' there should be the character 'bing' (troops)."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Senkai remarked, This sentence is especially obscure; perhaps the word bing (troops) should follow shuai.

sentences.zh: 」按也可能是衍文。

translations.literal: " Examining further, it may also be superfluous text.
translations.idiomatic: Alternatively, shuai may be a superfluous insertion.

sentences.zh: 延和二年衞大將軍樂安王範為雍州刺史詔式與中書侍郎高允俱為從事中郎 諸本「二年」作「三年」，「中郎」作「郎中」。

translations.literal: "In the second year of Yanhe, Defender-in-Chief Prince of Le'an Fan became Inspector of Yong province; an edict made Shi and Secretariat Gentleman Gao Yun together Staff Officers" — all editions read "second year" as "third year" and "zhonglang" as "langzhong."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yanhe Prince of Le'an Fan became Inspector of Yong province, and an edict appointed Shi and Secretariat Gentleman Gao Yun as his joint Staff Officers: all editions read the second year as the third year and zhonglang as langzhong.

sentences.zh: 按範為雍州刺史，見卷四上世祖紀上延和二年正月。

translations.literal: Examining: Fan as Inspector of Yong province appears in Basic Annals of Emperor Shizu, Part 1, juan 4, first month of the second year of Yanhe.
translations.idiomatic: Fan's appointment as Inspector of Yong appears in the Basic Annals of Emperor Shizu, juan 4, in the first month of the second year of Yanhe.

sentences.zh: 「三」字訛，今據改。

translations.literal: The character "three" is erroneous; now corrected according to evidence.
translations.idiomatic: The character for three is erroneous and is now corrected.

sentences.zh: 從事中郎是三公和將軍開府的屬官，卷四八高允傳也說「以本官領衞大將軍樂安王範從事中郎」。

translations.literal: Staff Officer was a subordinate post of the Three Excellencies and of generals who opened a headquarters; juan 48, Biography of Gao Yun, also says "with his original office he headed Staff Officer to Defender-in-Chief Prince of Le'an Fan."
translations.idiomatic: Staff Officer was a post under the Three Excellencies and under generals with their own headquarters. Gao Yun's biography in juan 48 likewise says he served as Staff Officer to Prince of Le'an Fan while retaining his original rank.

sentences.zh: 「郎中」是倒誤。

translations.literal: "Langzhong" is an inverted error.
translations.idiomatic: Langzhong is a transposed error.

sentences.zh: 今乙正。

translations.literal: Now transposed and corrected.
translations.idiomatic: The text is now corrected accordingly.
